noticias.titulo: Five Alpine destinations you can reach on new train routes this winter
noticias.resumen: From the French Alps to Austria’s historic mountain towns, these destinations offer everything from challenging ski runs to snowy walks, cosy restaurants and city sightseeing – with new and upgraded rail services making the journey easier.
noticias.texto:
From the French Alps to Austria’s historic mountain towns, these destinations offer everything from challenging ski runs to snowy walks, cosy restaurants and city sightseeing – with new and upgraded rail services making the journey easier.
The Alps offer plenty of reasons to visit in winter, even if you have no intention of putting on a pair of skis. Think pretty mountain villages, cosy restaurants, snowy walking trails and spectacular views.
Getting there is also becoming easier by train. For the 2026-2027 season, new direct rail links to Austria, upgraded sleeper services to Switzerland and the return of Eurostar Snow to the French Alps are opening up more ways to reach the mountains without flying.
For anyone keen to cut the carbon footprint of their winter escape, going by train is also a solid choice, as rail travel is far better for the environment than flying.
The experts at Rail Europe have picked out five Alpine destinations worth considering this winter, from resorts made for serious skiers to mountain retreats with plenty to offer those who prefer to keep their feet firmly on the ground.
The French Alps
The French Alps are a winter classic, whether you’re heading there to ski or simply fancy a few days in the mountains. Getting there is easier this season, too, with the return of Eurostar Snow and additional TGV services.
From 19 December, Eurostar Snow will connect Amsterdam, Schiphol Airport, Rotterdam, Antwerp and Brussels with six stations in the French Alps, including Moûtiers, Aime-la-Plagne and Bourg-Saint-Maurice.
There are also extra TGV INOUI services from France, with up to seven special trains running from Paris to Bourg-Saint-Maurice on peak days, as well as direct Saturday connections from northern France and services towards the Chamonix Valley.
Once there, Courchevel, La Plagne and Les Arcs are all within easy reach, and there's plenty to do beyond the slopes – from snowshoeing and winter walks to sledging, spa days and long lunches in mountain restaurants.
If you’re in Bourg-Saint-Maurice, try a seven-minute funicular ride which whisks visitors up to Arc 1600, a family-friendly, pedestrian-only village.
Innsbruck, Austria
If you’re keen to experience a city break with mountains on the doorstep, Innsbruck could be the place for you.
It’s going to be easier to get to the Austrian city next month, as a new daily direct ICE connection from Hanover, via Kassel and Würzburg, is set to launch on 13 December.
Innsbruck boasts a handsome medieval Old Town, traditional cafés and plenty of Tyrolean restaurants to explore. Be sure to visit the famous Golden Roof or, if you’re visiting from mid-November to the end of December, don’t miss the chance to wander around the city's Christmas markets.
An added bonus to this city is that the mountains are just minutes away. Its Nordkette cable cars, designed by Zaha Hadid, take visitors to around 2,300 metres in approximately 30 minutes.
Here, you’ll find steep, sun-soaked slopes – for all ability levels – as well as spectacular views across the city and the surrounding Austrian Alps.
St. Anton am Arlberg, Austria
St. Anton am Arlberg is one of Austria’s best-known winter resorts, drawing keen skiers with its challenging runs alongside a lively après-ski scene.
Getting there is set to be easier this season, with a seasonal ICE train connection from Frankfurt arriving on Saturdays and returning on Sundays from 13 December until 4 April.
The route continues along the scenic Arlberg railway to Landeck, opening up more of western Tyrol. Away from the slopes, visitors can explore winter walking trails, tuck into traditional Tyrolean food or spend an afternoon in one of the resort’s mountain bars.
Switzerland
Think of mountains, and you’ll probably think of Switzerland.
Getting there by train will soon become a more comfortable experience, thanks to upgraded Nightjet sleeper trains which will run from Amsterdam to Basel and Zurich, starting on 13 December.
Sleeping compartments and private mini compartments have been improved and make an excellent base for an overnight journey.
As well as exploring the delights of cities Basel or Zürich, travellers can also opt to continue towards the Swiss Alps by rail – and not an airport in sight.
Kitzbühel, Austria
Austria is seeing a particular boom in new routes this winter, and Kitzbühel is no exception.
The historic town may be best known for its famous Hahnenkamm ski race, but there’s plenty to enjoy here beyond the slopes.
Its medieval old town, with its colourful gabled houses, narrow cobblestone streets, and a 750-year history, is packed with traditional restaurants, cafés and shops, while winter walking routes offer a chance to take in the surrounding mountain scenery.
Getting there is more straightforward this season, too, with the seasonal ICE Großglockner set to run direct services from Hamburg and Hannover on selected weekends between 18 December 2026 and 4 April 2027.

noticias.titulo: 'Miracle on the Mississippi': All passengers rescued after tanker collides with cruise ship in New Orleans
noticias.resumen: According to the Port of New Orleans, all 197 passengers and crew members have been accounted for. "No critical injuries have been reported," it said in a post on social media.
noticias.texto:
According to the Port of New Orleans, all 197 passengers and crew members have been accounted for. "No critical injuries have been reported," it said in a post on social media.
All passengers on board a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after the vessel was struck by a tanker on Friday, officials have announced.
The American Heritage cruise ship, operated by American Cruise Lines, was docked at the Port of New Orleans when it was hit by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker, causing it to flip and become partially submerged.
"At this moment, the information that we have, we have zero people unaccounted for," New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told reporters, calling it a "miracle on the Mississippi."
"It was an all-hands-on deck approach, with harbor police responding first with just tremendous bravery going into the water even to start pulling people out," she said, while also commending firefighters and other ships in the area that provided assistance.
According to the Port of New Orleans, all 197 passengers and crew members had been accounted for.
"No critical injuries have been reported. Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by today's incident," it said in a post on Facebook.
Video footage circulating on social media shows the moment of the collision and the cruise ship going down.
Other footage shows people in life jackets swimming to safety as the vessel is on its side.
"What could have been a devastating tragedy instead demonstrated the courage, professionalism and extraordinary coordination of those who answered the call," the Port of New Orleans said.

noticias.titulo: EU leaders bring Italy and Poland into Ukraine peace talks team as Kallas fights for spot
noticias.resumen: Europe has decided on a joint team for the peace talks led by France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO. Despite mounting pressure, leaders declined to appoint a single envoy.
noticias.texto:
Europe has decided on a joint team for the peace talks led by France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO. Despite mounting pressure, leaders declined to appoint a single envoy.
European Union leaders have agreed on a joint team to represent Europe in the ongoing negotiations to end Russia's war on Ukraine, comprising France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom.
The UK is not an EU member but belongs to the E3 group.
The European Council, European Commission and NATO will also be represented.
The decision was taken on Friday at an informal summit in Dublin, Ireland, where the possibility of appointing a special envoy dominated discussions. Ukraine, the United States and even Russia had called on the EU to appoint a single representative.
Ahead of the meeting, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni had criticised the "disarray" of voices in the peace process and called for a single European envoy.
Instead, EU leaders opted to expand the existing negotiating group, adding Italy and Poland. Warsaw had pointedly warned against Western European countries making decisions on behalf of the East.
"We are fully engaged in supporting the ongoing process, and we hope it will deliver concrete results," European Council President António Costa said.
"The leaders agreed that our European team for the negotiations on peace in Ukraine is the European Union institutions and the E5 of the Coalition of the Willing."
The decision leaves EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas without the special envoy role she had publicly sought, as the diplomatic process increasingly sidelines her.
On Friday morning, Kallas made a forceful case for taking on the role, arguing that representing the bloc on foreign policy was part of her mandate.
"In June 2024, there was a decision by the leaders (on) who is representing (the EU) when it comes to security and foreign policy. And it was the discussion that in these five years there is going to be a negotiation with the Russians," she said.
"If the leaders want to change that agreement, of course, they may, because it is the leaders' decision, but I think we should focus our energy actually on the substance."
Kallas acknowledged that "Russians do not want me" because of her "strong" views.
Asked about her remarks, Costa appeared to dismiss her claim, pointing to the EU treaties.
"The treaties are very clear. The president of the European Council represents the European Council and represents the Union when it comes to the common foreign and security policy at the level of head of state and head of government," he said.
"The president of the European Commission represents the Commission, and the Commission represents externally the Union in community issues."
However, the negotiations have yet to reach the level of heads of state and government, taking place so far among national security advisers and senior officials.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also declined to back Kallas, despite her serving as a vice-president in the Commission.
"We decide on who represents us, and that's what we've done today, and how we are being represented to 27 sovereign countries plus the EU institutions," she said.
"We have taken our decision."
Friday's agreement largely formalises the negotiating format shaped by the United States, which is brokering the talks. The E3, EU institutions and NATO were represented at recent rounds of peace negotiations in Miami, Oslo, Brussels and Abu Dhabi.
Italy took part in the Abu Dhabi meeting. Poland is expected to join the next round.
"The E3 format has proven very effective. Incidentally, we always include Italy and Poland," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in Dublin, signalling that Berlin was not prepared to give up its seat in favour of a single envoy.
"In that regard, I don't see any need to have an institutional debate at the moment."
The key question now is whether Russia will agree to negotiate directly with European representatives, having repeatedly refused to sit at the same table as them.
US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Moscow on Thursday to persuade Russian President Vladimir Putin to engage. After the meeting, both said Moscow had indicated it was willing to hold face-to-face talks with Europeans.
But the Kremlin played it down, casting uncertainty over whether such a meeting will take place.

noticias.titulo: Russia sends major business delegation to Kabul for business talks with the Taliban
noticias.resumen: A Russian deputy prime minister led a 70-strong Russian delegation to Afghanistan, pursuing deals on transport, logistics, agriculture, and health products with the Taliban.
noticias.texto:
A Russian deputy prime minister led a 70-strong Russian delegation to Afghanistan, pursuing deals on transport, logistics, agriculture, and health products with the Taliban.
Russian deputy prime minister Alexei Overchuk was welcomed by a guard of honour when he arrived in Kabul on Thursday with a delegation of 70 Russian business people to conduct business talks with the Taliban government, Afghan officials said.
Overchuk met Taliban prime minister Mohammad Hassan Akhund, the deputy prime minister for economic affairs Abdul Ghani Baradar as well as foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.
According to a statement by the Afghan government published on X, Abdul Ghani Baradar described to the Russians Afghanistan's potential for economic development and investment, pointing to "strategic location, abundant resources and a workforce of 24 million people".
Abdul Ghani Baradar invited Russian companies to invest in agriculture, mining, constructions of roads, railways and factories, and to create a special economic zone in Afghanistan, while expressing his wish to expand exports of Afghan agricultural products to Russia.
The deputy prime minister also asked Russia to "provide the necessary facilities for Afghan products to be supplied to Russian markets and to cooperate in reducing transport and transit costs".
A Russian news agency quoted Alexei Overchuk as saying that the Russian delegation represent companies that are already operating in Afghanistan and that "many others want to start operating in this country."
Overchuk said that the companies represented in the delegation work in the fields of transport, logistics, agriculture and pharmaceuticals and that the Afghan government is interested in Russian chemical fertilisers, as well as in "building fertiliser production plants on Afghan soil".
Overchuk estimated that trade between Russia and Afghanistan in the first eight months of 2026 had more than doubled, reaching over 349 million dollars.
Russia officially recognised the Taliban government in July 2025, being the only state to have taken such a step since the Taliban seized power in August 2021, after the withdrawal of the United States.
Although no country other than Russia has formally recognised the new Afghan regime, the Taliban authorities have so far held high-level talks with many states and have established specific diplomatic and economic relations with some governments.

noticias.titulo: France and Germany near deal on De Cos for ECB top job as EU confirms two candidates
noticias.resumen: Two candidates are vying to succeed Christine Lagarde at the ECB, an EU official stated on Friday as EU leaders met in Dublin, while reports coming out of Spain said France and Germany are close to a deal on the central bank's top jobs with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as favourite for president.
noticias.texto:
Two candidates are vying to succeed Christine Lagarde at the ECB, an EU official stated on Friday as EU leaders met in Dublin, while reports coming out of Spain said France and Germany are close to a deal on the central bank's top jobs with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as favourite for president.
Two candidates have been put forward to replace Christine Lagarde at the helm of the European Central Bank, an EU official said on Friday, as EU leaders gathered in Dublin for an informal summit.
Spanish daily El País also reported that France and Germany were finalising a deal on the central bank's top jobs, with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as the favourite to become the next president.
The official did not name the two candidates, but as Euronews previously reported, the contenders are Pablo Hernández de Cos and former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot.
The Eurogroup confirmed both nominations last week.
European Council President António Costa updated leaders on Friday morning and aims to begin consulting the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council at the EU summit on 26 November, the official said.
A new deadline of 18 November has been set for nominations to fill the other two vacancies on the central bank’s six-member Executive Board, which runs the ECB day to day. The posts are chief economist and head of market operations, both significant roles in the leadership.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron are currently in "intensive" talks to negotiate the candidates.
In Dublin, Merz told reporters that agreements were in sight but not yet final, and that he needed a few more days to consult his coalition partners before presenting Germany's proposal next week.
Who gets what
France leans towards Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor whose more moderate stance on monetary policy suits a country under fiscal strain, El País reported.
He would be the first Spanish economist to lead the ECB.
Spain's Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo told Euronews on Monday that Hernández de Cos' expertise and ability to build consensus made him an ideal candidate.
The proposed deal would give Berlin the chief economist post and Paris the seat of Germany's Isabel Schnabel, who is in charge of market operations, German business daily Handelsblatt reported.
Merz's office wants Princeton University economist Markus Brunnermeier for the role, which is seen as the ECB's second most important job, the newspaper reported.
He would be the first German chief economist since Jürgen Stark left at the end of 2011, replacing Ireland's Philip Lane, whose term ends in May.
If Knot won the presidency instead, France would take the chief economist post and Germany would keep the market operations portfolio, Handelsblatt added.
Either way, a Franco-German deal would probably mean both posts would go to the eurozone's two biggest economies.
A German government spokesperson said Berlin wanted "adequate" representation in the ECB's leadership and expected a deal by the end of the year.
A vacancy in Basel
Picking Hernández de Cos would also free up the top job at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), where he has been general manager since 1 July 2025.
Owned by central banks around the world and based in Basel, Switzerland, the BIS is often called the "central bank of central banks".
His departure would create another senior vacancy, and the BIS Board of Directors would choose his successor.
With Schnabel due to leave the ECB on 3 January for a role at the IMF, three of the Executive Board’s six members are due to leave in less than five months.
Governments are therefore negotiating the posts as a package.

noticias.titulo: Iran MPs debate possible shift in nuclear doctrine and exit from NPT
noticias.resumen: Although the US midterm elections result appears to have reduced for now the prospect of a new full-scale US and Israeli attack on Iran, the fundamental US objective of stopping any Iranian nuclear programme is generating an intense debate in the Iranian society and its power circles.
noticias.texto:
Although the US midterm elections result appears to have reduced for now the prospect of a new full-scale US and Israeli attack on Iran, the fundamental US objective of stopping any Iranian nuclear programme is generating an intense debate in the Iranian society and its power circles.
Iran’s nuclear doctrine is generating a heated debate in the Islamic Republic’s parliament and power circles as the United States and Israel designated Iran’s capability to develop a nuclear weapon as the primary objective of their war on Iran.
Kamran Ghazanfari, a member of Iran's parliament, told Euronews on Friday that building nuclear weapons is far more essential for Iran that neutralising what he called “"US and Israeli propaganda against the Islamic Republic."
"When America and the Zionist regime have repeatedly threatened us with the use of nuclear weapons, we cannot be indifferent to this issue, as it is a threat that targets all the people of Iran and our very existence,” Ghazanfari said, adding that “they are enemies and have shown that they will not refrain from any crime so we cannot say 'God willing they will not use nuclear weapons against us'. We must confront them,” the Iranian lawmaker said.
He called on Iran’s leadership that “we must review the nuclear doctrine of the Islamic Republic so that the enemy knows that if it seeks a nuclear attack on Iran, it will face a reciprocal response from Iran,” adding that “just as since the Second World War until now none of the countries that possess nuclear weapons have used these weapons against each other because they fear that the other side will carry out such an attack against them, the Islamic Republic must also create deterrent power."
Ghazanfari does not see the lack of nuclear submarines and bombers capable of carrying nuclear weapons as undermining the Islamic Republic's nuclear deterrence, stating that missiles are also a solution to carry nuclear warheads.
But a former Iranian lawmaker, Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh, told Euronews that even if Iran had several nuclear warheads it would still lack nuclear deterrence, stating that "I find it unlikely that nuclear deterrence is part of our country's strategy because nuclear deterrence has three components: having an atomic bomb, a deterrent nuclear balance, and the ability to deliver the final blow. Those who think nuclear deterrence is created simply by having an atomic bomb are mistaken."
In a telephone call with Euronews, he said that "I really do not know whether the country has an atomic bomb or not, but, as far as I was aware, Iran's nuclear programme was peaceful, and even its possible military dimensions were closed by the JCPOA so that Iran's case would be removed from Chapter Seven of the UN Charter.”
“In my view Iran's military strategy is a conventional strategy, and this strategy has been fairly effective. I also find it unlikely that what Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei meant when he said that Iran has certain things was an atomic bomb," Falahatpisheh said.
Kamran Ghazanfari, however, believes that when the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council says that "we have something", he is referring not to an ordinary weapon but to a "special weapon".
He said that Iran is trying to formally withdraw from the Treaty of the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), the landmark international treaty whose objective is to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and weapons technology.
"I infer that this change of doctrine has in practice already happened. In parliament we are also pursuing withdrawal from the NPT, and last year some members of the presiding board of parliament blocked it, but MPs are still pressing for this plan to be put on the open floor, although a series of obstruction efforts are still preventing the plan from reaching the floor, Ghazanfari said.
But Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh considers the withdrawal from the NPT to be laying the groundwork for future wars against Iran, stating that "Iran's relations with the NPT have in practice been destroyed and whether Iran remains in the NPT or not depends on the nature of relations between Iran and America.”
“The discussion of Iran leaving the NPT does not help Iran's national interests because leaving the NPT amounts to hiding part of Iran's nuclear programme,” Falahatpisheh told Euronews, adding that Iran’s “Supreme National Security Council has not agreed to the MPs' triple-urgency bill to withdraw from the NPT, otherwise this plan would have been put before an open session of parliament."
Meanwhile on Thursday, Iran’s Assembly of Experts also called for examining the issue of Iran's withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
In a statement, the assembly, whose main task is oversight of the performance of the leadership, said that "examining the issue of withdrawal from the NPT, reviewing the country's defence doctrine and creating the necessary deterrence has become an unavoidable necessity and has turned into a public and national demand."
Finally, in announcing Iran’s latest position on the NPT membership, Iran's Foreign Ministry stressed that the Islamic Republic still remains committed to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.

noticias.titulo: Berlin clan boss Issa Remmo appears as 'state guest' at EU Parliament event
noticias.resumen: The head of the so-called Remmo clan in Berlin, Issa Remo, has officially joined a conference against Islamism in the European Parliament. This is fuelling debate in Germany and Brussels, and many are asking how this is possible.
noticias.texto:
The head of the so-called Remmo clan in Berlin, Issa Remo, has officially joined a conference against Islamism in the European Parliament. This is fuelling debate in Germany and Brussels, and many are asking how this is possible.
Clan boss Issa Remmo from Berlin took part in a conference of imams at the European Parliament in Brussels, as first reported by the Jüdische Allgemeine. The fact that the head of a clan, which in Germany is associated with an apparently endless list of offences, appears in Brussels as a state guest is seen as a slap in the face not only to the German justice system.
Photos show him listening to the speeches and applauding when the discussion turns to the fight against antisemitism. Yet his extended family in the Berlin district of Neukölln is hardly a symbol of successful integration and acceptance of Germany's basic values.
Serious crimes time and again
The 58-year-old is regarded in Berlin as the head of the so-called Remmo clan. The Remmo clan is estimated to have around 500 to 1,000 members, while the core family around its head, Issa Remmo, in Berlin, comprises around 103 people.
The immediate family circle around clan boss Issa Remmo lives predominantly in Berlin-Neukölln. Not all relatives are criminals. However, part of the extended family has repeatedly come to notice for serious offences. In 2023, five young men from the Remmo clan were convicted of the spectacular jewel theft from the Green Vault in Dresden.
Imam meeting in Brussels
According to information from the newspaper "Bild", Issa Remmo took part in the anti-Islamism conference at the EU Parliament at the invitation of French EPP politician Céline Imart and imam Hassen Chalghoumi. Chalghoumi is known as an interfaith bridge-builder and a clear opponent of terror.
The topics of the meeting were the fight against Islamism and antisemitism.
According to the report, the hosts initially knew nothing about Remmo's clan background. Imart later apologised to everyone who may have been hurt by his participation.
In the group photo of the organisation ELNET (European Leadership Network), which aims to improve relations between Europe and Israel and apparently organised the meeting alongside French conservative MP Céline Ismart, Remmo is clearly visible.
Jewish, Christian and Muslim religious representatives took part in the conference.
According to the Jüdische Allgemeine, Issa Remmo spoke in Brussels with French author of Jewish faith Marek Halter about antisemitism and said: "I am not an imam, but I can say one thing: we are all brothers in this world. Let us all live together, together. Where is the problem? Love will win, and terror will lose."
According to Remmo, there should no longer be any antisemitism, and Marek Halter agreed with "Inshallah".
Clan boss Remmo overshadows the Left party's election campaign in Berlin
Issa Remmo recently made headlines for attending an election party of the party Die Linke in Berlin-Neukölln. His son Firas is said to have communicated beforehand via chat with Left Party Bundestag member Ferat Koçak.
The Left party in Berlin-Neukölln insisted that it has neither political nor personal ties to Remmo. He stated in several conversations, including in Brussels, that he was disappointed with the Left party.

noticias.titulo: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 unveils shortlist of extraordinary nature images
noticias.resumen: From extreme close-up portraits of dragonflies to otherworldly mushrooms and some rather creepy crawlers, this year's shortlist offers a fascinating perspective into the hidden minuscule details of our world.
noticias.texto:
From extreme close-up portraits of dragonflies to otherworldly mushrooms and some rather creepy crawlers, this year's shortlist offers a fascinating perspective into the hidden minuscule details of our world.
The eighth edition of the Close-up Photographer of the Year (CUPOTY) competition has unveiled its shortlist, selected from a record 15,388 entries submitted by photographers around the world.
The images span 11 categories, including Animals, Insects, Arachnids and Underwater, alongside a dedicated category for young photographers.
“Close-up photography has a wonderful way of revealing details and perspectives that often go unnoticed,” says competition co-founder Tracy Calder. “This year’s shortlist is a fabulous showcase of imagination, technical expertise, and natural curiosity.”
The overall winner and category champions will be announced in January 2027. Until then, we've picked out some of our favourite images from the shortlist.
One word of warning before you scroll down further: if spiders make your skin crawl, you might want to look away for a couple of these.

noticias.titulo: Azerbaijan intensifies its European engagement at the EPC Summit
noticias.resumen: Azerbaijan added additional thrust to its engagement with Europe announcing more energy to the EU, a strategic partnership with the UK, additional agreements with Ukraine, a dozen bilateral meetings with European leaders and a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.
noticias.texto:
Azerbaijan added additional thrust to its engagement with Europe announcing more energy to the EU, a strategic partnership with the UK, additional agreements with Ukraine, a dozen bilateral meetings with European leaders and a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.
Azerbaijan is set to increase and diversify its energy supplies to Europe, beyond the current 10 EU member states, president Ilham Aliyev announced on Thursday during the 9th European Political Community Summit in Dublin.
Aliyev held talks with European Council President Antonio Costa during the EPC summit to discuss the long-term energy contracts “in the context of continuing successful cooperation between Azerbaijan and the European Union in gas supplies,” an Azerbaijani presidency statement said, while Costa declared that “the resumption of negotiations on a new EU-Azerbaijan agreement is good news for our citizens.” The EU-Azerbaijan Strategic Partnership in the Field of Energy was established in 2022.
Commenting on the meeting, Costa emphasized the two-way benefits of the EU-Azerbaijan cooperation declaring that “this has been an important year for EU-Azerbaijan relations,” adding that “with peace between Azerbaijan and Armenia now a reality, the EU is also investing to ensure that people across the region benefit.”
Aliyev said that Azerbaijan increased its gas supplies to the European Union from 8 billion cubic meters to 13 billion cubic meters, which accounts for nearly half of Azerbaijan’s exports, and that with the discovery of new fields, the South Caucasus country plans to increase gas supplies further.
The cooperation is now also focusing on renewable energy, a strategic national objective for Azerbaijan, with Aliyev highlighting the agreement reached between Azerbaijan, Georgia, Turkey and Bulgaria on exporting renewable energy to the European markets.
Azerbaijan’s president said that the gas pipeline stretching from Baku to Italy, passing through the territories of seven countries and supplying 10 European Union member states via interconnectors in Bulgaria, was currently operating at full capacity, and that Baku intends to continue expanding its transported volumes.
Costa and Aliyev also said that the European Union’s assessment of the Nakhchivan railway project would be completed soon and that they discussed the developments of transport links and connectivity within the global Middle Corridor project connecting Asia to Europe through the South Caucasus and Central Asia towards the Black Sea, a fast-developing alternative to the Strait of Hormuz crisis for the global supply lines.
Costa invited Aliyev to Brussels to continue the discussions on EU-Azerbaijan’s cooperation given the South Caucasus country’s role in Europe’s energy supply and security.
Strategic partnership with the UK
Azerbaijan’s president Ilham Aliyev and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed a Joint Declaration on Strategic Partnership between Azerbaijan and the United Kingdom, during the EPC Summit in Dublin.
With the UK being the largest European investor in Azerbaijan’s economy, historically driven by BP's Caspian operations, the new strategic framework focuses on defence and security cooperation, expanding trade and investment, renewable energy, infrastructure as well as artificial intelligence, advanced technology and others.
British officials said relations have now reached a historic milestone and both leaders committed to expanding mutual trade, defence cooperation, and private-sector investment ties under the new accord.
With Russia watching on, the UK and Azerbaijan agreed to “strengthening cooperation in defence and security in support of regional peace and stability” (...) “across a broad spectrum of security priorities, in response to evolving security challenges and threats.”
The two sides also agreed to “support the development of the Middle Corridor, alongside transport, logistics and infrastructure projects that facilitate cross-border trade and investment.”
Securing the Ukrainian grid and drone agreements
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a “detailed discussion” with President Aliyev during the EPC summit, focusing on emergency support for Ukraine's battered energy grid ahead of the harsh winter and post-conflict reconstruction strategies.
Zelenskyy confirmed that contracts were signed under the so-called “Drone Deal,” an ongoing bilateral drone agreement, saying that “we are working to scale up orders,” adding that “relations between our countries are developing.”
Zelenskyy also thanked Aliyev for Azerbaijan's humanitarian assistance as officials confirmed an ongoing €1.35 million emergency grid support package from Baku, comprising heavy electrical equipment and generators.
Total Azerbaijani humanitarian aid to Ukraine has now reached €48 million, focusing on civilian energy infrastructure and medical rehabilitation.
Ukraine’s president also noted that Kyiv is closely analysing Azerbaijan's post-conflict reconstruction across Karabakh and the East Zangezur regions, as the Ukrainian government views Baku's massive infrastructural overhaul as a viable blueprint for its own eventual post-war recovery.
The two leaders also discussed expanding economic and trade relations, including private-sector economic cooperation, with Zelenskyy saying that “we value the fact that companies are staying and continuing to work for our people, often despite Russia’s vile attacks.”
Advancing the Armenia-Azerbaijan peace process
Building on their historic peace process, Azerbaijan’s president Ilham Aliyev held new talks with Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan on advancing their peace consolidation, border delimitations, water cooperation and interconnection of electricity grids as well as more confidence-building measures.
The two leaders also discussed the progress of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) connectivity project, including the planning of its railway and highway components.
Since November 2025, a total of 105,000 tonnes of cargo have been transported to Armenia through the territory of Azerbaijan.
Broadening European engagement
President Aliyev met with Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis for talks on upgrading the Southern Gas Corridor's infrastructure in the context of Azerbaijani-Greek bilateral relations, anchored by the Trans Adriatic Pipeline (TAP).
Aliyev also held talks with Moldovan President Maia Sandu on energy cooperation and on strengthening Moldova’s energy security as well as economic and trade ties with a particular focus on the agricultural sector.
Azerbaijan’s president met his Romanian counterpart Nicusor Dan for the first time to discuss energy and connectivity projects, focusing on linking the Caspian and the Black Seas.
Dan said in a post on X that “we focused on deepening our Strategic Partnership, advancing key energy and connectivity projects, and pursuing an ambitious shared political and economic agenda,” adding that “our cooperation, linking the Caspian and the Black Sea, has strong potential to grow.”
Aliyev also held energy talks with Bulgaria’s prime minister Rumen Radev and Czech prime minister Andrej Babis.

noticias.titulo: Estonia accuses Russia of attempted arson attack on defense firm
noticias.resumen: "Estonia is preparing for the possibility of closing its border with Russia," said Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal.
noticias.texto: Estonia has accused Russia’s military intelligence service of ordering an attempted arson attack on an Estonian drone maker, prompting Tallinn to threaten to close its border with Russia. Intruders were found at Threod Systems in Viimsi, outside the Estonian capital, shortly after 3 a.m. on Saturday trying to break into the building with the aim of setting it on fire and causing an explosion, Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said Sunday. Writing on X , Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said: “This is part of Russia’s broader hybrid war against Europe, with the aim of decreasing support to Ukraine and pressure on Russia. We will not be intimidated.” He added that “Estonia is preparing for the possibility of closing its border with Russia to reduce the risks to our people and national security.” Threod’s security staff stopped the attack before it could cause significant damage, authorities said. Eight suspects, all residents of neighboring Latvia, were detained. Five have been remanded in custody. Estonia’s Internal Security Service, known as KAPO, said intelligence gathered by its officers showed the attack was commissioned by Russia’s GRU military intelligence agency. Threod makes long-range reconnaissance and attack drones. “We will not be intimidated. Together with our allies, we will continue supporting Ukraine and standing firm against Russian aggression,” Estonia’s defense ministry said in a statement on X. The latest attempt follows an August arson attack on Milrem Robotics, which supplies unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine. Estonian authorities formally blamed Russian intelligence for that incident in September. KAPO has warned that Russia is increasingly targeting European defense manufacturers to disrupt military production and deliveries to Ukraine. The investigation into Saturday’s attempted attack remains ongoing.

noticias.titulo: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships
noticias.resumen: Three commercial vessels were hit near Romania’s coast, prompting fighter jet deployments and fresh calls for NATO support to strengthen Black Sea security.
noticias.texto: Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu on Sunday condemned drone strikes on three commercial ships near his country’s Black Sea coast, promising to work with NATO allies to strengthen security in the region following the latest attacks. “These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law,” Niculescu said in a post on X. He added that Russia’s war against Ukraine was causing the security situation in the Black Sea to deteriorate. The ships were hit Saturday evening and overnight near Sulina, a Romanian port where the Danube River meets the Black Sea. The Greek-flagged oil tanker Evia Petrol V was struck just after 9 p.m., followed 35 minutes later by a strike on another ship, the Marsol, according to a statement from Romania’s defense ministry published on its Facebook page. “In both cases, the fires were extinguished by the ships’ crews. No casualties were reported,” the ministry said. A third vessel, the Ali Najafov, also reported being struck overnight. It remains unclear who launched the drones. Romania’s military detected aerial targets on radar and sent F-16 fighter jets into the air. Authorities also issued warnings to residents near the coast about possible drone threats. The attacks came after another commercial ship, the Larissa 1, was reportedly hit by a drone near Romania’s coast on Friday. Romanian Defense Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea said Sunday he would raise the incidents with allied counterparts in Brussels. “We need the solidarity of our allies,” he said, calling for more surveillance aircraft and equipment to defend against drones. Last week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the EU will help finance some Black Sea security costs following recent attacks on commercial shipping. In October, at least seven commercial vessels were struck by drones in the Black Sea close to NATO and EU members Romania and Bulgaria, leaving more than 20 sailors dead and dozens missing.

noticias.titulo: Israel kills Hamas commander in Gaza strike
noticias.resumen: Samir Abu Younis, who helped plan and oversee the Oct. 7 massacre, took control of Hamas' Rafah Brigade just two months ago.
noticias.texto: Israel said Sunday it had killed a senior Hamas commander in an overnight airstrike in southern Gaza, just two months after his predecessor was killed. The Israel Defense Forces identified the commander as Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, who led Hamas’ Rafah Brigade and reportedly had a leading role in planning the Oct. 7 2023 massacre in Israel. “Abu Younis was appointed commander of the brigade approximately 2 months ago, following the elimination of his predecessor,” the IDF said in a statement posted on X on Sunday. According to the Israeli military, Abu Younis previously served as deputy commander of the brigade and led its Tel al-Sultan Battalion. The IDF accused him of directing attacks against Israeli civilians and soldiers, as well as working to rebuild Hamas’ military capabilities. “The terrorist was eliminated in order to remove the threat he posed,” the military said. Writing on Telegram , Hamas’s Al-Qassam Brigades said Abu Younis had been involved in “numerous high-profile operations” and was “one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the October 7th attack.” Abu Younis succeeded Nael Abu Obeid, who was killed by Israel on Sept. 15, making him the latest in a series of Hamas commanders targeted by Israeli forces. The killing comes amid a fragile ceasefire that took effect in Oct. 2025, ending major fighting but failing to stop Israeli strikes in Gaza. U.S. President Donald Trump’s broader peace plan remains stalled over disagreements about Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has insisted that Hamas surrender its weapons before Israeli troops withdraw, rejecting a proposed phased approach that would see both steps take place in parallel.

noticias.titulo: Ukraine claims thousands of Russian casualties and a slowing Kremlin advance
noticias.resumen: Ukraine is countering Russia's narrative of battlefield success by blunting the Kremlin's attacks.
noticias.texto: DNIPRO, Ukraine — Heavy Russian losses are one of the reasons for Moscow’s slowing advance in Ukraine this year, the commander of the country’s Air Assault Forces said. “Even though the Russian offensive continues, the enemy is not demonstrating rapid operational successes that would allow it to advance quickly. They are slowing down,” Maj. Gen. Oleh Apostol told a group of journalists in a secure location on Tuesday. “If they capture a single tree line in a month, that hardly constitutes an operational success upon which further gains can be built,” Apostol said. Russian casualties are rising, according to the commander and to NATO officials. “In the past few months, Russia has been losing more than 40,000 troops — killed or seriously wounded — every month. The United States in 14 years, in Vietnam, lost 56,000. Here in one month, Russia, dead or seriously wounded, 40,000. And in October, early reporting indicates this number may have climbed to over 50,000,” NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said this week. Neither Ukraine nor Russia publishes their exact military losses. The Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies this summer estimated that Russian forces had suffered about 1.4 million casualties, including 400,000 to 450,000 fatalities, from the start of the full-scale invasion through June 2026. It estimated Ukrainian casualties at 525,000 to 625,000, including 125,000 to 150,000 fatalities, over the same period. Despite rising casualties, the Russian military continues to press forward but is making few lasting gains, Apostol said. He estimated that Ukrainian forces had retaken more than 800 square kilometers from Russian forces this year as the result of two local counteroffensive operations. Ukraine’s offensives have both a military and a political meaning as they show Kyiv is successfully resisting Russian pressure, Apostol said. In his view, successes on the battlefield provide additional arguments for continuing military aid from Kyiv’s allies, while a lack of positive momentum could increase external pressure to negotiate. “Ukrainian counter-offensive actions refute Russian claims regarding the impossibility of further resistance and strengthen Ukraine’s arguments in its engagement with international partners,” the general said. Apostol said that many of Moscow’s claimed successes are propaganda efforts that do not mark real territorial gains and that lower-level commanders may mislead their superiors about the actual situation on the battlefield. When it’s impossible to demonstrate real success, Russian forces use individual soldiers with flags to film proof of control over entire areas, Apostol said, adding that such soldiers are usually quickly killed by Ukrainian forces. “A Russian flag at a given position does not necessarily mean that the location has actually been captured and is being held,” he said. Claims and counter-claims During the latest round of U.S.-led peace talks this week, Russia claimed it had occupied half of the territory in the Donbas that is currently under Ukrainian control, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said . “So the Russians think and they share that they really occupied half of the territory of Donbas, which we control really,” he said, adding that Russian leader Vladimir Putin was being misinformed and that Kremlin negotiators were trying to use exaggerated territorial claims to influence the U.S. “I think that Putin lives a little bit in different information,” Zelenskyy said. “It’s a different reality. And of course, he is sharing with America.” Russia is claiming that it has taken 6,500 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory this year, while the Institute for the Study of War think tank estimates that the real total is a Russian net gain of only 73 square kilometers. Putin is “trying once again to breathe life into the myth of inevitable Russian military victory in order to persuade the United States and other supporters of Ukraine to compel Kyiv to surrender,” ISW wrote. Apostol underlined that Ukraine is being very careful in its operations to try and minimize troop losses because of its lack of manpower. “You must attack where success is possible,” Apostol said, adding that Ukraine favors localized attacks instead of a massive counteroffensive. In many cases, the goal is to stabilize the frontline and not to take more territory. “Launching an offensive against a well-prepared enemy force that holds a numerical advantage may fail to yield the desired outcome,” he said. Ukraine has a much smaller population than Russia and has had difficulties in recruiting new forces and preventing soldiers from deserting. “If a person is treated like a dog, they might go AWOL,” Apostol said.

noticias.titulo: EU reiterates ‘grave concern’ over Gaza humanitarian crisis as winter approaches
noticias.resumen: The bloc's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has called on Israel to allow more humanitarian aid into Gaza as weather worsens living conditions.
noticias.texto: Europe’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has called on Israel to protect civilians in Gaza as severe flooding batters the enclave, saying an airstrike on the Nasser Hospital on Thursday was “deeply alarming.” “The severe flooding and winter conditions that have struck Gaza are further aggravating the living conditions of an already exhausted population, exacerbating unsafe conditions and human suffering,” Kallas said in a statement Saturday. Kallas also called on Israel to comply with international law and allow the United Nations and humanitarian organizations unimpeded access and to reopen all border crossings into Gaza. “After a year since the ceasefire was announced, military strikes continue and shortages of essential items, including suitable shelter, medicine and medical equipment, caused by the existing access restrictions persist, resulting in the absence of acceptable and dignified living conditions,” Kallas’ statement said. Israel denies breaching international law and blocking humanitarian aid. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended the amount of aid allowed into Gaza. He said Israel was supporting winter preparedness in Gaza but wouldn’t allow terror group Hamas to exploit humanitarian supplies. Israel’s Foreign Affairs Minister Gideon Sa’ar severed ties with Kallas in June after a media report alleged she compared Israel to apartheid South Africa. Kallas has long backed a push from several member countries to pressure the European Commission to ban trade with territories illegally occupied by Israel. Israel’s mission to the EU was reached for comment. Israel launched the war in Gaza in response to Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack that killed about 1,200 people and in which 250 people were taken hostage. Since then, more than 70,000 people have been killed in the Palestinian enclave.

noticias.titulo: Italy hits Meta with €805m fine over privacy law violation
noticias.resumen: It is the largest fine ever issued by Italy's data protection regulator.
noticias.texto: Italian authorities fined Facebook’s parent company Meta €805 million for using photos and videos from Android phones without users’ specific consent, the Italian Data Protection Authority said in a statement Saturday. The fine concerned the “camera roll suggestions when browsing Facebook” feature, which suggests photos and videos from a phone’s gallery for users to add to posts. The feature violates the Italian law implementing the EU’s ePrivacy directive, the authority said. It is by far the largest fine ever imposed by the Italian regulator. The investigation, launched in 2025, established that access to a user’s camera roll is requested with a single permission for the entire app, which the authority said covers multiple features with different needs. The authorization request was preceded by a generic warning that didn’t allow users to understand that they were authorizing picture and video suggestions, the authority said. “If granted in full, this type of permission allows the app to read the device’s entire photo archive, usually permanently, without the user or the authorities being able to verify which information is actually being used,” the statement reads. The authority also said it “rejected the objection of lack of jurisdiction raised by the company in favor of the Irish authority, because the ePrivacy regulation does not provide for the ‘one-stop-shop’ mechanism.” Meta has 60 days to get consent separately and specifically for the feature, clearly explain what it does and how it can be disabled, the authority said. It also must be disabled by default, including for those who have already authorized it. Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. It has the right to appeal the decision.

noticias.titulo: Nearly €20m in cash found buried, hidden in Hungary corruption case
noticias.resumen: Hungarian authorities investigating a former minister for corruption say they uncovered a trove of hidden cash.
noticias.texto: Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly €20 million in cash buried in forests, hidden in warehouses and residential properties and stored in a high-value safe as part of a bribery investigation into a former minister. The money was found during searches on Thursday and Friday as part of a criminal investigation into former minister Miklós Seszták, who worked under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, relating to bribery allegations. ​Seszták, who is under pre-trial detention has denied wrongdoing. Hungarian Prime Minister Peter ‌Magyar launched a wide anti-corruption campaign after ousting Orbán earlier this year. The money — more than 5 billion forints, €2.6 million and €1.2 million — was found across locations in Budapest, Pest, Békés and Nógrád counties, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office, an anti-corruption body, said in a statement . “This officially marks the end for the Fidesz-KDNP mafia!” Magyar posted on Facebook , originally in Hungarian, in reference to Orbán’s government. It took 12 Treasury staff eight hours to tally the cash using 5 counting machines, Finance Minister Kármán András said. The announcement comes after Hungarian authorities detained Aron Orbán, the former prime minister’s brother, as part of an investigation into people smuggling. The former prime minister said on social media that the move, announced by Magyar on Monday, was part of a “political witch-hunt” to get him. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reacted wryly to the latest announcement, referring to the arrest of Orbán’s brother and the cash discovery on X . “Dear Victor, I’ve always been an admirer of your creativity, but now I must say I’m impressed as never before,” he wrote.

noticias.titulo: US suggested Ukraine could give up Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
noticias.resumen: "This was the first time this had been raised," the Ukrainian president told reporters.
noticias.texto: The U.S. has floated the idea of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for withdrawing from its eastern Donbas region as part of negotiations to end the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Friday. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelenskyy told reporters on Friday, a day after he met with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Dublin . The Donbas region in Ukraine’s far east borders Russia, and Moscow declared it had annexed the region in 2022 after its full-scale invasion. The vast majority of the region is occupied by Russian troops. Giving up Donbas has long been part of the proposals put forward by U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration, including the 28-part plan for a peace agreement proposed by the White House in 2025 . Russian President Vladimir Putin has previously demanded that Ukraine abandon its efforts to join NATO and accept strict limits on the size of its military. “I have said repeatedly: Ukraine is not retreating and is not giving up its land to terrorists,” Zelenskyy told reporters. The White House and U.S. State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Zelenskyy said he was discussing a “comprehensive security package” with partners that would include specific guarantees from NATO and the EU, a strong Ukrainian army with adequate troops, weapons and financial support for a set period and a recovery plan with clear funding attached. “If the American side confirms precisely this to us, together with other NATO partners, then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own,” Zelenskyy said. “Of course, this would be without any recognition of the occupied territories as Russian,” he added. “But we need specifics, and we don’t have them yet. All of this is still under discussion,” the president said. Veronika Melkozerova contributed to this report.

noticias.titulo: Finland rejects reported Russian demand to leave NATO as part of peace talks
noticias.resumen: "This is absolutely outrageous to even suggest such a thing," Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen said.
noticias.texto: Finland has rejected a reported Russian demand that it leave NATO as part of Ukraine peace talks, with Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen saying its membership in the alliance wasn’t up for negotiation. “Such matters are in no way a matter for negotiation. Russia knows that. This is absolutely outrageous to even suggest such a thing,” Häkkänen told reporters on Friday , according to Finnish broadcaster Yle. Finland, which shares a 1,340-kilometer border with Russia, joined NATO in 2023 in a foreign policy U-turn prompted by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. German newspaper Bild reported that a Russian proposal made during talks in Abu Dhabi this week included Moscow keeping occupied Ukrainian territories, gaining control of new swathes of land, demilitarizing ports in Ukraine, removing NATO bases from the Baltics, and Finland leaving NATO. Russia proposed withdrawing its nuclear weapons from Belarus and refraining from stationing intermediate-range missiles there in exchange, Bild reported. But it remains unclear which proposals Russian President Vladimir Putin would support after discussions between intermediaries, according to the report. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a new security framework for Europe for after the war raised by the Americans “can be dangerous.” “Russia certainly cannot make decisions on behalf of all the societies that are members of NATO,” he told reporters on Friday. Zelenskyy’s comments were not in direct response to the demands reported by Bild, but came after a meeting between Zelenskyy and U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Thursday in Dublin . “Putin’s desire to change borders in Europe is a fact. I am sure this is part of his concept of revising security guarantees in Europe. This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said.

noticias.titulo: ‘Not apathy but disconnection’: We asked Europe’s youngest MEPs what they thought of the continent-wide Gen Z protests
noticias.resumen: From Porto to Athens, Europe was taken by surprise by the mass youth protests for better education, an affordable cost of living, and political accountability. EUobserver spoke to 12 of the youngest MEPs in the European Parliament to understand the issues at the heart of Gen Z unrest.
noticias.texto: From Porto to Athens, Europe was taken by surprise by the mass youth protests for better education, an affordable cost of living, and political accountability. EUobserver spoke to 12 of the youngest MEPs in the European Parliament to understand the issues at the heart of Gen Z unrest. One topic that has been largely misunderstood is political engagement. “It is not the apathy some attribute to Gen Z, but a disconnection from the political establishment, because it is not delivering for them,” said Lena Schilling, a 25 year-old Austrian MEP for the Greens. For instance, an EU study from October found that 55 percent of young Europeans had participated in at least one social initiative. The issue is that “fewer political candidates take an interest in young people,” 34-year old German Socialist & Democrat (S&D) MEP Delara Burkhardt told EUobserver. The average age of MEPs is 50, with the largest demographic in the parliament being men in their forties. Older people also make up an increasing proportion of those voting in Europe. Read more Listen: Is the right to protest under threat in Europe? It’s a “huge structural shift, [meaning] young people don’t feel listened to or represented,” said French S&D MEP Chloé Ridel, aged 34. The very few elected to speak on behalf of young people have “to elbow our way through our own committee.” Europe has seen wave after wave of youth-led protests in the last two months, starting with French high-school students demanding better education, bringing up to 600,000 people to the streets and continuous protests since 17 September. The French were followed by the Spanish housing movement, culminating in the first general strike in 14 years, counting some four million workers and close to 200,000 protesters across the country. The movement spread from Madrid to squares in Rome, Lisbon and beyond, as students and neighbours hoisted tents in central areas to protest the cost of living. The discrepancy between those elected and those electing , has resulted in a vast chasm in priorities – and language. The weekly protests erupting from every corner of the continent received responses of “warning of chaos and disruptions to public order, instead of addressing the legitimate reasons behind people’s dissatisfaction,” said 33-year old Czech Green MEP Markéta Gregorová. noticias.titulo: Nuclear weapons – the elephant in the room in Ukraine peace talks
noticias.resumen: Since February 2022, president Vladimir Putin has used tacit and overt nuclear threats to try to achieve tactical advantage in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. And now there are no guardrails. For almost a year, the United States and Russia have had no binding limits on their strategic arsenals.
noticias.texto: American, Ukrainian and Russian negotiators have restarted peace talks with a limited agreement to swap prisoners of war. But Jared Kushner, president Donald Trump’s envoy, says Washington is working on “a broader European security architecture” built on five goals: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term stability. Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, agrees, calling for a wider European security arrangement before a deal to end the Ukraine war. European capitals have been alarmed, and with reason. Read more Trump vows ‘beautiful’ Russia deal, as EU agonises over which envoy to send to Ukraine peace talks The future security of a continent is being discussed with a government that is still bombarding Ukrainian cities every night. European governments are trying to insert themselves into the talks and seemingly now have US backing. If a new order for Europe is being drawn up, Europeans should insist on writing into it the one word absent on Kushner’s list: nuclear. It is a striking omission, because every one of his five goals is at heart a nuclear question. Crisis communication, transparency and escalation risk matter so much precisely because this war is being fought – and tensions with Moscow are increasing – in the shadow of the bomb. The gravest danger of the past five years has never been confined to the front line in Ukraine. It is that a nuclear-armed state has used the threat of mass destruction to try to keep others from coming to the aid of its victims. Since February 2022, president Vladimir Putin has used tacit and overt nuclear threats to try to achieve tactical advantage in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. And now there are no guardrails. For almost a year, the United States and Russia have had no binding limits on their strategic arsenals. Who nuclear deterrence really rewards Defenders of nuclear deterrence say it keeps the peace. This war shows what it actually does. Russia felt emboldened by its nuclear arsenal to launch a full-scale invasion. Its nuclear weapons were not a shield against aggression. They were the arms holding the spear. Nuclear deterrence is a contest over who is more believably prepared to kill millions. A system that pays out to whoever appears most reckless is not a source of stability. It is an incentive to aggression. A path to disaster. This is why any settlement of this war matters far beyond Ukraine. If the terms of peace reward territory seized under nuclear coercion, the message will be heard by every would-be proliferator. Europe must not copy Moscow’s playbook Europe’s current response risks mirroring the logic it fears. In March, president Emmanuel Macron announced the first increase in France’s nuclear arsenal in more than three decades and launched a still undefined “forward deterrence” concept. Macron has also had himself photographed watching the test launch of a ballistic missile from a submarine accompanied with bellicose rhetoric, eliciting satirical comparisons with the North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Read more Lithuania moves to lift ban on nuclear weapons as ‘Russians do not attack the strong’ The fear behind these moves is understandable. But they accept Moscow’s rules of the game: a competition in conveying a credible threat of assured destruction that nobody wins, and in which the risk of miscalculation only grows. More nuclear weapons in more places is not a security architecture. It is a shorter fuse on the same bomb, and the continent seems willing to hand Vladimir Putin a match What Europe should put on the table If Washington wants to talk about European security, Europe should answer with concrete nuclear demands: First, declare nuclear threats inadmissible. In 2022, G20 leaders, following the lead of states that have joined the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, agreed that the use or threat of use of nuclear weapons is inadmissible. Any framework for European security should turn that principle into a binding commitment, with consequences for breaking it. Second, Europe can no longer host the nuclear chessboard of Russia and the US. Russian weapons in Belarus should be removed; as should the US weapons in six European countries. After that, interim verified limits to nuclear weapons must be agreed. Greater military transparency must mean warhead numbers and inspections, not just notifications of exercises. Finally, the elimination of nuclear weapons must be anchored in law that already exists. The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons , already signed or ratified by a global majority, bans not only the use and possession of nuclear weapons but also the threat to use them. Read more Putin and the threat of a tactical nuclear attack In three weeks, countries meet at the UN for the treaty’s first review conference. European governments that want a security order resistant to blackmail should be in the room, at the very least as observers. Moscow and Washington cannot dictate Europe’s future. Neither should nuclear threats, whoever makes them. A peace that leaves the bomb as the final arbiter of borders is not a lasting peace. It is a pause before the next blackmail attempt.

noticias.titulo: EU leaders hand Ukraine peace talks to France, Germany, UK, Italy, Poland plus Brussels – instead of a single envoy
noticias.resumen: As EU leaders began debating who speaks for Europe in Ukraine peace talks, a senior diplomat said sending EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas was “just not possible”.
noticias.texto: EU leaders agreed at their informal summit in Dublin on Friday that Europe will be represented in Ukraine peace talks by the EU institutions together with France, Germany, the UK, Italy and Poland, rather than a single envoy. “Today, the leaders agreed that our European team for the negotiations on peace in Ukraine is the European Union institutions and the E5 of the ‘Coalition of the Willing’,” European Council president António Costa told reporters after the meeting on Friday (13 November). Under the arrangement, the EU will take the lead on Ukraine’s “European future, its reconstruction, and prosperity”, while security guarantees “must be addressed within the framework of the coalition of the willing, in close coordination with Nato”, Costa said. “Europe must speak with one clear and united voice in all discussions that shape the future of Ukraine and the security of our continent,” he added. Read more Trump vows ‘beautiful’ Russia deal, as EU agonises over which envoy to send to Ukraine peace talks The decision largely formalises the current arrangement, in which France, Germany and the UK sit at the table alongside Italy and Björn Seibert, chief of staff to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen. Earlier on Friday, a senior diplomat called that set-up “not ideal”. It also leaves open whether foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas will take a seat. EU capitals did support sending her to the talks, the diplomat said, adding that it was “just not possible”. ‘Setting traps’ Kallas, for her part, defended her role as she arrived at the summit, and warned that Russia was “setting traps” by trying to divert attention from its aggression with a debate on Europe’s security architecture and the role of Nato. noticias.titulo: Russian aviation’s losing streak continues, with three aircraft and their crews lost near St Petersburg (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,723)
noticias.resumen: A night that cost Russia three of its own aircraft, a Ukrainian pilot felling nine drones with a single F-16 sortie, and a supposed humanitarian corridor that could help Moscow tighten its grip on Kostiantynivka together paint a war where every tactical success hides a dangerous twist.
noticias.texto: A MiG-31, Ka-52, and Mi-8 crashed while repelling an air raid, prompting speculation that the friend-or-foe identification system was compromised. Russian combat helicopters account for the largest share of Ukrainian drones being shot down. Ukrainian F-16s are equally indispensable in intercepting Russian unmanned aircraft. Putin proposed repeating in Kostiantynivka the humanitarian operation modelled on Oleshky — but there are fundamental differences between the two cities. Maps of the day — Kostiantynivka Videos of the day — an attack on the bridge across the Mius River; Kyiv residents flee a burning trolleybus struck by a drone. A MiG-31, Ka-52 and Mi-8 crashed while repelling an air raid, prompting speculation that the friend-or-foe identification system was compromised. Reciprocal air raids have become so commonplace that it is impossible to report on their consequences every day. It remains the case that while Russia mainly attacks energy infrastructure, Ukraine primarily targets refineries and oil-industry facilities. Both armies are inflicting serious damage on each other. Ukrainian cities, however, are suffering far more. On Wednesday, however, a particular air raid targeted the area around St Petersburg, including the Ust-Luga oil terminal. The entire area has been the target of intensive air raids. Among other things, Ukraine this week struck a Russian missile corvette in the Baltic Sea , while several radars were reportedly hit on Wednesday: 🔥Three Russian radar systems were struck during Ukraine’s massive drone attack on Leningrad Oblast on November 11, according to Dosye Shpiona. ●Nebo-SVU long-range surveillance radar ●40V6 mobile radar tower ●Sopka-2 airspace surveillance radar complex pic.twitter.com/qUtqSxZYCk — Special Kherson Cat 🐈🇺🇦 (@bayraktar_1love) November 13, 2026 But the greatest interest was generated by the crash of three military aircraft, in which seven crew members died. “Defending our skies has never cost so much in a single night,” the Voevoda Broadcasts channel wrote . “Defending the skies over St Petersburg from drone attacks has cost us dearly today. Very, very, very dearly,” the well-known aviation channel Fighterbomber admitted on Wednesday evening. It gave no details, but this time others did so on its behalf. noticias.titulo: ‘Very overdue’ – MEPs welcome proxy voting for pregnant members and new mothers
noticias.resumen: An overwhelming majority in the European Parliament agreed MEPs can delegate their vote to another member in the months before and after childbirth, retaining their say in key files.
noticias.texto: An overwhelming majority in the European Parliament has agreed that MEPs can delegate their vote to another member in the months before and after childbirth, retaining their say in key files. The statute change, passed with 578 votes for, 25 against, and 4 abstentions on Thursday (12 November) will mean that an MEP will be able to vote for one other colleague for three months before, and six months after, childbirth. It is “well overdue” that the rules for voting change, Sigrid Friis, a Renew Europe MEP from Denmark told EUobserver. She herself worked up until her due date, provoking some comments about the need for a midwife in the parliament. “No member should lose her right to vote because of becoming a mother,” declared the parliament’s president Roberta Metsola in a statement back in April. Read more MEPs discuss proxy voting for pregnant women and new mothers Delegating one’s vote would only apply for the plenary sessions, with both the absent MEP and the one voting for them would be identified in the minutes for transparency’s sake. Maria Ohisalo, a Finnish Green MEP, told EUobserver she is “really happy” about the reform. “I voted for hours with our baby in the plenary,” she said, recalling her infant was not eligible for child care during the first Strasbourg plenary after giving birth. Another MEP who preferred to stay anonymous recalls some colleagues’ annoyance at taking multiple breaks during trilogue negotiations when she was with her newborn. The initiative, started by parliament president Roberta Metsola in 2025, still needs an EU Commission opinion and a go-ahead from the council before a final vote in the parliament.

noticias.titulo: [Interview] ‘Do not be afraid, be prepared’: Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal on how to defend Europe from Russia
noticias.resumen: Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal lays out how to build up Europe's defences. He also urges the use of Russian assets frozen in Belgium, and discussed Baltic expertise in fighting Vladimir Putin.
noticias.texto: First published in Respekt. Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal has laid out how to build up Europe’s defences. He also urges the use of Russian assets frozen in Belgium, and discusses Baltic expertise in fighting Putin. The liberal leader spoke with Ondřej Kundra in early November. Has anything brought you satisfaction recently as a politician? Kristen Michal: I recently attended the opening of Estonia’s largest timber building in northern Estonia. It may sound amusing this would bring joy to a prime minister, but in my previous role as environment minister, I launched this project in 2023. It is a truly beautiful area, both in nature and culture – I recommend visiting. It has a maritime museum in a former seaplane harbour, as well as Estonia’s only submarine. And beside it stands the largest wooden building of its kind: our new natural history museum, under whose roof we want to bring together institutions focused on ecology and climate. It is not merely a wooden structure; it is also probably one of most cost-effective buildings, amounting to about €2,100 to €2,200 per square metre. One of our state agencies began its construction, and I was genuinely emotional at the opening ceremony – it is rewarding for a politician to see that something they started was actually completed. Estonia is one of the foresighted Baltic member states which has warned for years about the Russian threat. EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen has recognised that Baltic warnings about Russian expansionism unfortunately came true… I would probably have been happier if Baltic states had not been right. We spoke about Russia in the past, warning that Putin had imperial dreams of restoring the Soviet Union, that he was not concerned solely with Ukrainian territory, but also with stripping Ukraine of its sovereignty, or that he had further territorial ambitions. It would of course have been preferable if our warnings had not been proven wrong. But they were proven right. Even before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, you warned the West about energy dependence on Russia and about unpreparedness for cyber threats. Now, Europe has learned its lesson. Are you satisfied that EU member states have woken up to reality, or do you think they remain blind to such threats?
