noticias.titulo: No new Yalta: Russia’s demands ignore the facts on the ground
noticias.resumen: The latest Russian proposals for ending the war in Ukraine have been widely compared to ...
noticias.texto: The latest Russian proposals for ending the war in Ukraine have been widely compared to a new Yalta Conference – a grand bargain in which Moscow would secure a huge zone of influence in a revised European security order, including a rollback of NATO to its 1997 borders. The analogy is historically and strategically flawed. In 1945, Stalin’s Soviet Union sat at the table as the largest army fighting Hitler, its advance into Central Europe so rapid that it unsettled both Washington and London. Today’s Russia is the aggressor, unable to advance meaningfully in Ukraine and, by multiple accounts, losing ground in areas it previously occupied. Putin’s Russia is not in a position to dictate terms. At Yalta, the Red Army’s momentum was the central fact. Stalin’s USSR (which included Ukraine) had carried the heaviest burden against Nazi Germany, and Western leaders negotiated with an eye toward containing further Soviet expansion while still needing Soviet cooperation to finish the war. The resulting spheres of influence reflected battlefield realities more than abstract principles. Putin’s Russia occupies the opposite position. Its full-scale invasion of Ukraine has produced a grinding war of attrition in which Russian forces have failed to achieve decisive breakthroughs. Reports of Ukrainian counter-advances and the reclamation of previously held territory underscore the gap between Russian rhetoric and military performance. Treating Ukraine as a state on the verge of collapse, or the West as prepared to accept a strategic surrender, does not match the observable balance of forces. Ukraine’s political resilience further undermines the Russian case. Despite the enormous costs of war, Kyiv has maintained institutional continuity and a clear chain of political authority. Russia, by contrast, has managed the conflict through intensified domestic controls, economic adaptation under sanctions, and a leadership style that may be questionable, while remaining consistent with the constraints of martial law. The image of a stable, ascendant power imposing terms on a faltering neighbor is difficult to sustain when the aggressor appears more brittle politically than the country it is attacking. Russian insistence on returning NATO to its 1997 footprint effectively asks the Alliance to reverse decades of enlargement and accept a permanent zone of diminished security on its eastern flank. This demand frames the West as the party that must make the larger concession, as it the West was capitulating, akin of Nazi Germany: a huge manipulation of the type only the Kremlin can fabricate, and only Trump’s administration can accept. Clearly, no major Western capital, if any, has indicated willingness to rewrite the post-Cold War settlement on Moscow’s terms. The readiness of a Trump-led United States to engage with elements of the Russian narrative does not alter the fundamental constraint: any durable settlement requires Ukraine’s consent. Peace cannot be imposed over Kyiv’s objections without risking the collapse of the arrangement the moment Russian pressure eases or Ukrainian capabilities recover. Post-war security arrangements likewise cannot be designed without the European Union and the United Kingdom. Both have direct interests in the stability of the continent, substantial economic exposure, and, in the case of several EU members, shared borders or immediate proximity to the conflict zone. Europe’s recent decision to field a seven-person negotiating team has drawn understandable criticism for projecting disunity and bureaucratic caution. The optics are poor. At the same time, the European approach still reflects a basic recognition that sustainable security in Europe cannot be negotiated solely between Washington and Moscow. When both the Kremlin and parts of the American political spectrum appear willing to test or discard established constraints, the European insistence on process and consent, however cumbersome, functions as a stabilizing element rather than pure obstruction. None of this guarantees a near-term breakthrough. Negotiations remain difficult because the core issues – territory, security guarantees, and the long-term status of Ukraine – remain far apart. A “black swan” event, whether a sudden military shift, a major political change inside Russia, or an unexpected alignment among Western capitals, could compress the timeline. In the meantime, history is not going to repeat itself in the manner Moscow appears to prefer. Caption: The “Big Three” at the Yalta Conference, February 1945, Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin. Behind them standing, from the left, Field Marshal Sir Alan Brooke, Fleet Admiral Ernest King, Fleet Admiral William D. Leahy, General of the Army George Marshall, Major General Laurence S. Kuter, General Aleksei Antonov, Vice Admiral Stepan Kucherov, and Admiral of the Fleet Nikolay Kuznetsov. [Photo credit: U.S. military photographer, name unknown]

noticias.titulo: Drone strikes commercial vessels in Romanian territorial waters
noticias.resumen: This article has been updated, with plural added in the title (vessels from vessel) to ...
noticias.texto: This article has been updated, with plural added in the title (vessels from vessel) to reflect official confirmation from Romania’s Ministry of National Defence of two further drone strikes on commercial vessels inside Romanian territorial waters near Sulina on the evening of 14 November. The Greek-flagged tanker EVIAPETROL V was struck around 21:10 local time, approximately four nautical miles east-southeast of Sulina, causing a fire that the crew extinguished. Roughly 35 minutes later, the St. Kitts and Nevis-flagged bulk carrier MARSOL was hit about five nautical miles southeast of the Sulina Canal; a fire also broke out on board and was put out by the crew. No casualties were reported in either incident. These events follow the confirmed 13 November strike on the Palau-flagged general cargo vessel Larissa 1 (detailed below), which sustained damage to a cargo crane but reported no injuries or fire. Romanian authorities continue to investigate the origin of the drones. Reports of a possible third vessel (ALI NAJAFOV) being struck in the same period remain unconfirmed by Bucharest. 🇷🇴 🚨BREAKING: THREE MORE COMMERCIAL VESSELS REPORTEDLY STRUCK IN ROMANIAN TERRITORIAL WATERS Following Friday’s drone incident involving LARISSA 1, three additional commercial vessels were reportedly struck inside Romanian territorial waters on Saturday evening. • 🇬🇷… pic.twitter.com/UqQLX1bNhP — Coffe Report (@CoffeReport) November 15, 2026 —– A commercial vessel sailing under the flag of Palau was struck by an aerial drone on the evening of Friday, 13 November 2026, in Romania’s territorial waters approximately 12 kilometres (roughly 6.8–7 nautical miles) north-northeast of the town of Sfântu Gheorghe in Tulcea County. The ship, identified as the general cargo vessel Larissa 1 (IMO 9154268), was heading toward the Sulina roads with a final destination in Ukraine. Romanian authorities confirmed the incident the following day, stating that no crew members were injured and that no fire broke out on board. According to reports from Digi24, HotNews, and other Romanian outlets citing local sources including Ziua de Constanța and TVR Info, the attack was reported around 21:40. The vessel’s captain informed Romanian naval authorities at Sulina that the drone damaged only a cargo crane used for loading and unloading operations. The Maritime Coordination Centre of the Romanian Naval Authority made contact with the ship to assess the situation. The Larissa 1, a roughly 149-metre vessel built in 1999 with a deadweight capacity of about 17,000 tonnes, continued under its own power after the strike. Official Romanian response Defence Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea, who was in Constanța’s military port on Saturday conducting a working visit, publicly confirmed the incident. He stated that he had been informed overnight, that there were no wounded or fatalities, and that the damage was limited to the crane area. Oprea emphasised that Romanian authorities continuously monitor objects detected on the water or near national airspace and that at least two air alerts had been issued in Tulcea County on Friday. He noted ongoing coordination between the Ministry of National Defence, the Romanian Naval Forces, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Coast Guard. An investigation into the origin and circumstances of the drone remains underway, and the minister declined to speculate on its provenance pending further checks. Romanian Air Force F-16s on air-policing duty were scrambled on Saturday morning after radar detected an aerial target near Snake Island (Insula Șerpilor). This followed the Friday evening incident and reflected the heightened surveillance posture in the western Black Sea. Romanian pilots have previously downed multiple drones that entered national airspace or territorial waters in recent months. Wider pattern of attacks on shipping The strike on the Larissa 1 fits a pattern of attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea linked to the war in Ukraine. Romanian media noted that the western Black Sea has seen repeated incidents affecting ships heading to or from Ukrainian ports. In late October, the defence ministers of Bulgaria, Romania, and Turkey condemned recent attacks on merchant shipping and agreed to establish a coordination mechanism for maritime security. Separately, reports on 14–15 November described additional drone strikes near the Sulina anchorage involving other vessels, including the Greek-flagged tanker Eviapetrol V and the bulk carrier Marsol (Saint Kitts and Nevis flag). Fires broke out on those ships but were controlled by their crews, with no casualties reported. These events underscored the persistent risk to navigation in the area. EU maritime security hub and regional measures The incident coincides with accelerated efforts to strengthen Black Sea maritime security. On 9 November, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, during a visit to Bucharest, announced that the EU would allocate €50 million to speed up the creation of the Black Sea Maritime Security Hub, with complementary centres in Constanța (Romania) and Varna (Bulgaria). From Bucharest Von der Leyen vows EU response to Black Sea attacks An additional €10 million was earmarked for rapid reaction and search-and-rescue operations. The hub is intended to improve information sharing, early warning, protection of critical infrastructure (ports, submarine cables, pipelines, and offshore installations), and resilience against hybrid and cyber threats. Romanian officials have indicated that work on the command centre is already underway, with the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs (via the Coast Guard) expected to play a leading role in coordination, supported by the Ministry of National Defence for surveillance and intervention capabilities. Defence Minister Oprea has stressed continuous monitoring and the readiness of Romanian and allied assets, including aircraft from air-policing missions, to detect, deter, and, if necessary, engage threats. The Romanian government has repeatedly summoned Russian diplomats over previous incidents and has intensified air and maritime surveillance. As of 15 November 2026, the investigation into the Larissa 1 strike continues. No official attribution of the drone has been made public by Romanian authorities. Attacks on commercial ships inside the territorial waters of a NATO country remain uncommon, even amid the recent rise in drone strikes in the western Black Sea. Such an incident could lead the affected ally to request NATO consultations under Article 4 if it judges that its territorial integrity or security is threatened. Caption: Undated photo of the commercial ship Larissa 1 [Maritime Traffic]

noticias.titulo: Hungarian authorities find nearly 19.5 million euros buried by Orbán minister
noticias.resumen: Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash – some of it buried in ...
noticias.texto: Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash – some of it buried in forests or hidden in buildings and safes – during a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, a former minister in Viktor Orbán’s government. The National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) announced the find after coordinated searches on 12–13 November 2026 in Budapest and the counties of Pest, Békés, and Nógrád. Investigators located large quantities of banknotes buried in woodlands, concealed in farm buildings, warehouses, and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location. The recovered cash totaled 5,071,632,000 Hungarian forints, €2,658,350, and $1,257,100, valued at approximately EUR €19-19.5 million depending on exchange rates at the time. The money was deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury; Finance Minister András Kármán said a dozen treasury employees spent eight hours counting it using five banknote-counting machines. 💰This is what €17.7m in cash looks like. It was buried in a forest and hidden in safes and rural houses. Hungarian investigators found HUF 5,071,632,000, €2,658,350 and US$1,257,100 while investigating a close ally of Viktor Orbán, former development minister Miklós Seszták. pic.twitter.com/3f3ZFQtXlV — Szabolcs Panyi (@panyiszabolcs) November 14, 2026 Seszták served as Minister of National Development from 2014 to 2018 under Orbán. Prosecutors suspect him (and Norbert Szivek, then CEO of the state asset manager Magyar Nemzeti Vagyonkezelő) of receiving more than 11 billion forints in unlawful benefits between 2015 and 2018 through an intermediary from companies linked to the state bus operator Volánbusz. The probe involves allegations of overpriced purchases of more than 600 used buses (reportedly causing roughly 10 billion forints in losses to state firms) and other state-related deals. Seszták has denied wrongdoing. He is under pre-trial detention; his lawyer has stated that the seized cash does not belong to him and noted that the case involves other suspects. His parliamentary immunity was lifted in late September, after which he was detained. The recovery is part of “Operation Purgatory,” the anti-corruption campaign launched by Prime Minister Péter Magyar after his centre-right Tisza party defeated Orbán’s Fidesz in the April 2026 elections, ending 16 years of Fidesz-led rule. Magyar described the cash haul on social media as marking “the end for the Fidesz-KDNP mafia.” Fidesz responded that it hoped Seszták was not connected to the money and that the party could not associate itself with anyone who failed to uphold the law. A recent poll indicated strong public support for the anti-graft efforts. This is one of several investigations into former Orbán-era officials. Separate probes have led to the arrest of other ex-ministers and former central bank chief György Matolcsy on graft-related accusations; all have denied wrongdoing. The NVVH was established under the new government specifically to pursue cases involving alleged misuse of public funds from the previous period. The discovery has drawn international attention as a concrete example of the new administration’s push to recover assets and investigate alleged systemic corruption during Orbán’s long tenure. Seszták remains in custody as the investigation continues. Caption: The stash appearing on photo posted by Prime Minister Péter Magyar on X

noticias.titulo: Zelenskyy: US raised Donbas withdrawal for NATO membership; issue returns to talks
noticias.resumen: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators have for the first time asked whether Kyiv ...
noticias.texto: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators have for the first time asked whether Kyiv would withdraw its forces from the parts of Donbas it still controls in exchange for Ukraine joining NATO. He described the idea as evidence that NATO membership has returned to the negotiating agenda, while stressing that no concrete proposal exists yet and that Ukraine will not cede territory. Speaking to journalists on 13 November (remarks published the following day), Zelenskyy stated: “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time.” He repeated his long-standing position that “Ukraine does not retreat and does not give its lands to terrorists.” He said Kyiv is discussing a comprehensive security package with partners that would include concrete guarantees from NATO and the EU, sustained support for a strong Ukrainian army (defined troop numbers, weapons and financing for a set period), and a Prosperity Plan for reconstruction backed by clear funding sources. “If the American side confirms this to us together with our other NATO colleagues, then I will ask the opinion of our society: do we accept it or not? I have no right to do this at my own discretion,” Zelenskyy said. He added that any arrangement would not involve recognising occupied territories as Russian and that specifics are still lacking. Zelenskyy also noted that European partners, including French President Emmanuel Macron, Denmark and Nordic countries, argue that Ukraine’s battle-hardened forces would significantly strengthen the Alliance. “They cannot simply let Ukraine go after such defence support, the development of our army and the strength of our defence. And they need Ukraine in NATO because then the Alliance will become many times stronger,” he said, concluding that “NATO is back on the agenda.” The comments follow trilateral talks involving Ukraine, the United States and Russia in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, mediated by the U.S. Ukrainian officials described the format as constructive on humanitarian issues and security guarantees, while Russian representatives said discussions focused on Europe’s future security architecture. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff also met Zelenskyy in Dublin around the same time. Russia’s official position has remained consistent and maximalist. Moscow has repeatedly rejected Ukrainian NATO membership as a “red line,” demanded a demilitarised or neutral status for Ukraine, and called for NATO forces to return to the Alliance’s 1997 borders (i.e., before the post-Cold War enlargements that brought in former Warsaw Pact countries and the Baltic states). These demands have featured in Russian statements throughout the full-scale invasion and the latest rounds of diplomacy. International outlets including Reuters and the BBC confirmed Zelenskyy’s account of the U.S. question linking a Donbas withdrawal to potential NATO membership. Kyiv continues to insist that any settlement must rest on robust, lasting security guarantees rather than neutrality, which Zelenskyy has said would require changing Ukraine’s constitution. This article draws on coverage by EUalive’s partners Suspilne and European Pravda Caption: Zelenskyy speaks to the press on 13 November 2026 [Suspilne]

noticias.titulo: EU leaders hold first high-level AI talks in Dublin, agree on European team for Ukraine peace talks
noticias.resumen: European Council President António Costa said on Friday that EU heads of state or government ...
noticias.texto: European Council President António Costa said on Friday that EU heads of state or government held their first in-depth discussion on artificial intelligence at an informal summit in Dublin, while also agreeing on a joint European approach to Ukraine peace talks. Hosted by Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin during Ireland’s Council presidency and chaired by Costa, the meeting at the Convention Centre Dublin followed the previous day’s European Political Community summit. Costa thanked Martin for the “warm Irish welcome” and described AI as “the most important technology of our time.” He stressed that Europe must maximise its benefits for productivity and public services while managing risks and helping set global standards for safe, human-centric AI. Leaders heard from two external guests: Arthur Mensch, CEO of French AI company Mistral, and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton (Physics, 2024), whose research underpinned modern AI systems. Discussions covered two strands: boosting Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty, and addressing AI’s societal impacts, safety, and trust. On competitiveness, Costa highlighted Europe’s strengths in talent, research, and start-ups, but said translating them into advantages depends on mobilising public and private investment for competitive models, securing value chains to reduce dependencies, and ensuring access to affordable clean energy. He pointed to existing tools such as the Savings and Investments Union and the proposed “28th regime,” as well as the decisive role of the next EU long-term budget, particularly the European Competitiveness Fund. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen added that Europe already leads in AI adoption – 37% of EU businesses used AI in 2025 on average, with Finland at 66% (nearly double the US rate). She outlined plans for industrial AI via Special Envoy Jim Snabe, 19 AI factories, and seven AI gigafactories mobilising around €30 billion in computing capacity. She estimated at least €500 billion is needed overall for technological sovereignty, including chips, compute, and frontier models, and said the Commission would follow up with ambitious financing proposals. Mensch reportedly urged redirecting substantial spending on foreign tech toward European infrastructure. On risks, Costa underlined that clear oversight is essential for public trust, noting that the EU is the first region with a comprehensive AI governance framework (the AI Act) and should use that experience in the G7, G20, UN, and with the upcoming UK presidency. Leaders examined impacts on fundamental rights, children, democratic processes, labour markets, the European social model, market concentration, and cybersecurity. Hinton issued strong warnings about “runaway AI” and existential risks. Costa said the topic will return at the leaders’ retreat in Alden Biesen on 5 February 2027 and will be the central theme of the 2027 Social Summit marking the 10th anniversary of the European Pillar of Social Rights. Ukraine dominated much of the day despite the AI focus. Leaders agreed that Europe’s negotiating team for peace talks will comprise the EU institutions plus the E5 countries of the Coalition of the Willing (France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and the United Kingdom). Costa stated: “Europe’s security begins with Ukraine’s security.” He welcomed diplomatic efforts, insisted on a just and lasting peace based on principles of European security, and noted that only Ukraine can decide on its territory and sovereignty. Security guarantees fall to the Coalition of the Willing in coordination with NATO. The next formal European Council on 26–27 November will address Ukraine’s financing needs for 2027 and beyond, based on Commission proposals; von der Leyen also signalled a 22nd sanctions package against Russia. News reports described the Ukraine representation debate – sparked in part by Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s concerns over fragmented formats – as overshadowing the AI agenda, with leaders settling on a team-based compromise rather than a single envoy. Costa emphasised unity and close coordination so Europe speaks with one voice. Witkoff: Next meeting of the teams is already scheduled; Europeans will be present The informal format produced no formal conclusions, but Costa described the AI exchange as the first of several, with further work ahead on investment, adoption, governance, and societal impacts. The agreement on a seven-member European negotiating team – the E5 national governments plus the European Commission and Council – is widely viewed by analysts as a setback for Kaja Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs, and more broadly as a dilution of the institutional role of the Union’s foreign-policy chief. An extraordinary video as EU chiefs Antonio Costa and Ursula von der Leyen effectively throw Kaja Kallas under the bus after a question about her claim that she'd been chosen to represent the EU in negotiations with Russia. Costa delivers a short lecture on the EU treaties,… pic.twitter.com/fNhTxYqPXw — Brian McDonald (@BrianMcDonaldIE) November 14, 2026 Let's be clear about what happened today in Dublin: National leaders definitively killed the EU foreign policy chief role created in 2009 but undermined ever since. From now on, the world will know this isn't a real role and the EU is not serious about foreign policy. A tragedy. — Dave Keating (@DaveKeating) November 13, 2026 Caption: Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin (L) and President of the European Council Antonio Costa attend a final press conference at an informal European Council meeting in Dublin, Ireland, 13 November 2026. EU leaders gathered in the Irish capital to discuss European competitiveness, artificial intelligence sovereignty, and AI’s societal, security, and economic impacts, alongside the latest developments in Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. EPA/OLIVIER HOSLET

noticias.titulo: U.S. to resume flights after air traffic network failure sparks chaos
noticias.resumen: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications ...
noticias.texto: The Federal Aviation Administration ( FAA) lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at ​U.S. airports and triggered the longest shutdown since the 11 September 2001 attacks. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said U.S. airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (0115 GMT), ‌but warned that departures would resume gradually and it would take time for airlines to restore normal operations. “It’s going to be slow,” Duffy told reporters at the White House. More than 6,600 flights were canceled and 8,600 delayed, with another 1,500 already canceled for Sunday, according to FlightRadar24. Aviation analysts said the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline schedules for days. Duffy said tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports around the country. Duffy said he ​and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office to discuss the outage. The failure is the latest and most dramatic sign of ​strain on a U.S. air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers. Duffy said the ⁠trouble began at 3:36 p.m., when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar and communications systems. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they started to give us inconsistencies ​in the data from those routers and because of that we shut the system down,” Duffy said, adding that at no stage did they completely lose radar or communications and they were able to safely land thousands ​of planes. Duffy said the immediate problem had been fixed and that flying was safe, but warned that a broader overhaul of the aging air traffic control system was needed to prevent similar failures. $50 billion aviation overhaul Duffy blamed Congress for failing to fund a new system that he said could prevent such outages, and called for $50 billion to modernize it. Earlier on Friday, before the outage, the White House and Department of Transportation had urged Congress ​to approve $30.1 billion to upgrade the nation’s aging airports and air traffic control infrastructure. “What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system,” Duffy said. “Give us the money to fix it.” Homeland ​Security Secretary Mullin said there was “zero evidence” so far that the outage resulted from a cyberattack or a rogue AI system, though investigators had not ruled out either possibility. “It appears this was mechanically driven, however, we’re still ‌looking,” Mullin said. The ⁠National Security Agency was working with the Department of Homeland Security on the investigation, he added. The outage appeared to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to two airline officials. The network handles critical radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers to communicate with pilots. L3Harris did not respond to a request for comment. Pain nor over for passengers Though the ground stop was lifted, the disruption for passengers was far from over. From Boston to Seattle and New York to Los Angeles, passengers crowded departure halls and airline desks as delays and cancellations mounted and aircraft ​remained parked at gates. Thousands of passengers faced being ​stranded overnight. Edward Kargbo, 50, from West Chester, ⁠Pennsylvania, had been scheduled to take a 9 p.m. Ethiopian Airlines flight to Lomé, Togo. Instead, he planned to spend the night at the airport before a rescheduled flight at 6 a.m. on Saturday. “I have to squat the night here,” he said. “I’m stranded.” Louise Maher, 47, was also caught up ​in the disruption at Newark after her British Airways flight to London was caught up in the aviation meltdown. “I might cry at some ​point but not yet,” she ⁠said. U.S. airlines will not be required to provide compensation to stranded passengers because the carriers were not responsible for the FAA system failures. The only other nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks came in January 2023, when the FAA halted domestic departures for about 90 minutes. Investors were already pricing in a financial hit to airlines. Shares of American Airlines, United Airlines and Delta Air Lines fell between 1% and ⁠2% in after-hours ​trading, while JetBlue Airways dropped about 3%. American Airlines said it was prioritizing flights to smaller cities outside its major ​hubs and international destinations to position aircraft and crews for a faster recovery. With Reuters Caption: Southwest Airlines passengers line up to speak with a customer service representative after their flight was canceled at Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA, 13 November 2026. Communications failures at all 22 regional air traffic control centers forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to order a nationwide ground stop. EPA/CHRIS TORRES

noticias.titulo: Russia reportedly demands Finland exit NATO in sweeping Abu Dhabi proposals
noticias.resumen: German newspaper BILD broke the story on Friday that Russian negotiators presented far-reaching informal proposals ...
noticias.texto: German newspaper BILD broke the story on Friday that Russian negotiators presented far-reaching informal proposals during recent U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the war in Ukraine and establishing what the paper described as a “new European security order.” The demands, which BILD said originated from within President Vladimir Putin’s inner circle and were shared with European representatives, go well beyond Ukrainian territory. According to the report, Moscow proposed retaining all currently occupied Ukrainian territories and taking full control of the Donbas, including the Kyiv-controlled parts of Donetsk and Luhansk. Ukraine would be required to adopt permanent non-aligned status, ruling out NATO membership while leaving open the possibility of joining the European Union. The ports of Odesa and Mykolaiv would be demilitarized and barred from use as naval bases, with separate arrangements guaranteeing freedom of navigation in the Black and Baltic Seas. The proposals also call for NATO to abandon military bases in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, and for Finland – which joined the alliance in 2023 – to leave and return to its pre-membership status. On Moldova, the plan envisions transforming the country into a federal republic including Moldova proper, Gagauzia, and Transnistria; if Moldova joins the EU, Transnistria and Gagauzia could hold independence referendums. In exchange, Russia reportedly offered to withdraw nuclear weapons from Belarus, abandon intermediate-range missiles there, and pull troops from Transnistria. The talks themselves took place on 10-11 November in Abu Dhabi and marked the first trilateral meetings involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States since February. U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff participated, with European representatives present on the sidelines. The sessions produced agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange but no broader breakthrough; US officials described the discussions as productive on practical issues such as monitoring a potential ceasefire. Kremlin denial Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov quickly denied the most striking element of the report. “I am not aware of this. No, no such conditions have been put forward. This definitely was not discussed,” he told reporters, according to Russian media. Peskov’s comments specifically addressed the Finland demand; Moscow has long argued that Western countries once promised not to expand NATO eastward and continues to seek written guarantees against further enlargement. BILD noted that the document was one of several unofficial drafts circulating and that it remained unclear whether Putin had personally endorsed this version. Finnish and regional reactions Finnish officials rejected the reported demands outright. Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen called the idea of Finland leaving NATO “absolutely outrageous” and non-negotiable. “Such matters are not open to negotiation under any circumstances. Even suggesting something like that is absolutely outrageous,” he told reporters. Häkkänen added that Russia has pushed similar sphere-of-influence ideas for years, including in its 2021 ultimatums before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and appears to be testing Western resolve by expanding the scope of talks beyond Ukraine. Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen and others signaled that Helsinki views the reports as further evidence Russia is not seriously committed to a limited peace deal focused on Ukraine. Baltic states have likewise treated any restrictions on NATO presence on their territory as non-starters. The BILD report, though difficult to verify independently and denied in key respects by the Kremlin, largely restates longstanding Russian maximalist positions that would amount to the effective capitulation of Ukraine through permanent territorial losses, enforced neutrality, and severe limits on its future security choices. What is new is that, if genuine, these proposals also demand that the West itself capitulate by reversing core elements of its post-2022 security architecture, including Finland’s NATO membership and the alliance’s military presence in the Baltic states. Caption: Head of the Russian delegation Vladimir Medinsky (L) speaks during a trilateral talks between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the US, in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, 10 November 2026. EPA/ALTAF QADRI / POOL

noticias.titulo: Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes
noticias.resumen: Old-school technology including telephones, faxes and ​Bluetooth limited the damage for some people on Friday ...
noticias.texto: Old-school technology including telephones, faxes and ​Bluetooth limited the damage for some people on Friday as a worldwide outage of Microsoft’s Outlook left millions without email. The prolonged ‌disruption, which also hit Microsoft Teams and Copilot, affected some of the world’s biggest institutions, from bankers and traders to shipping firms. While most reported their core systems were still running, trading and administrative work slowed in places in the latest reminder of how much of the world’s commerce, public services and communications run on a handful of technology providers. “The pressure is ​mounting to invest in contingency plans and test whether those backups actually work when needed,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore, adding that ​firms needed multiple providers for key services like communication and data storage. Microsoft, which says on its website that more than ⁠430 million people use its 365 services, blamed server problems and said it was not aware of any malicious activity. Organisations that host Microsoft services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared. The outage is one of the longest in Microsoft’s history and the second disruption to its services this year. Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online – its ​cloud-based email and scheduling hub – leaving unconnected applications operational. The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure ​that underpins it. The disruption comes weeks after attacks on the ​industrial systems that keep supermarket food cold and shows how a single point of failure, whether a technical fault, cyberattack or even an extreme weather event, can ​disrupt everyday business. In its latest update on Friday, Microsoft said it was seeing signs of stabilisation after implementing fixes more broadly to attain a persistent recovery of services. European exchange operator Euronext, which runs bourses in Paris, Brussels, Lisbon, Amsterdam, Oslo, Athens and Milan, told listed companies to pick up the phone. “We have ensured that the team has sufficient capacity to manage ​the situation and handle the additional workload,” a spokesperson said, adding that Euronext was verifying the identity of callers to protect confidentiality and integrity. Aviva, which ​reported earnings on Friday, said it had put backup plans in place, including sending out alternative phone numbers for earnings calls and using Bluetooth to transfer recordings because email ‌was down. The ⁠British insurer tested a similar-scale outage of its most critical technology systems about two weeks ago, CEO Amanda Blanc told Reuters. Shipping group Maersk asked customers to call with anything urgent and urged them to verify any unexpected communications about the outage with their local representative. Fax machines return in Taipei In Taiwan, the outage disrupted fund management at securities firms, life insurers and investment trust companies, people familiar with the situation said. At another financial firm, trades such as purchases and sales ​of short-term bills, which are normally ​confirmed by email, had to be ⁠confirmed by fax instead, one of the people said. Foreign banks and financial institutions in Taiwan were hit especially hard, a trader said, because much of their data is emailed to overseas headquarters through Microsoft’s systems. In Britain, HSBC and Barclays ​activated internal incident teams to assess the impact, people within the banks told Reuters. While email systems were down, ​most client services were ⁠unaffected. HSBC reminded staff not to use unauthorised channels such as personal email or WhatsApp to get around the outage, one said. Two trading professionals said they observed lower trading volumes in some markets on Friday that they attributed to difficulties in executing trades. Caitlin Egen of Control Risks said that big global firms usually had contingency plans, ⁠but when ​key services went down abruptly it was still a “wake-up call”. “For a lot of businesses this ​morning, it’s probably been chaos trying to figure out how to even get in touch with people,” she said. With Reuters Caption: A device shows the Microsoft logo as the Teams software displays an error message on a laptop, in London, Britain, 13 November 2026. US multinational technology company Microsoft has been working to fix a global outage affecting some of its services, such as Teams, Outlook, and its artificial intelligence software, Copilot. The services are experiencing ‘connectivity problems’ caused by ‘elevated load’ on their infrastructure. The outage’s effects are being felt in at least 74 countries across the world, with schools and the National Health Service affected in the UK. EPA/NEIL HALL

noticias.titulo: Bulgarian parliament bans breeding of animals for valuable fur
noticias.resumen: In a rare display of near-complete unanimity, members of parliament have banned the breeding of ...
noticias.texto: In a rare display of near-complete unanimity, members of parliament have banned the breeding of animals for their fur. Violations of the ban will be punishable by fines of up to €10,000. The prohibition ensures that mink, chinchillas, foxes, raccoon dogs and other animals will no longer be raised and killed in Bulgaria solely for their pelts. The bill was prepared with the assistance of the association “Kazhi” (Say), which notes that Bulgaria is among the countries supporting the European Citizens’ Initiative “Europe without Fur.” The initiative’s goal is a ban on fur farms and on the import of fur products across the entire European Union. In 2022, volunteers from the organisation “Invisible Animals” revealed in a BTV report the horrors behind the walls of a mink farm in the Stara Zagora region. The animals were confined in cramped, dirty wire cages with no room to move, and were killed by carbon dioxide gassing, which is considered a humane method of euthanasia. Residents living near the farm had to endure the terrible smell that spread through the area, while domestic animals became victims of the small predators that escaped from captivity. In 2025, the Supreme Administrative Court finally upheld the ban on breeding American mink in Bulgaria. The order had been issued by the Ministry of Environment and Water at the end of May 2022 but was appealed by the owners of the country’s only such farm. It was owned by “Farmpro,” whose partners include Ivan Angelov, his son Angel Angelov and relatives better known for the “Gradus” poultry brand. In the end, the farm was closed. “Today we can say not only that the country’s only fur farm has closed its doors, but that such an unprecedentedly cruel practice will never again have a place in Bulgaria, thanks to the legal amendment just adopted. This is further proof that change is possible and that the efforts of civil society matter,” said representatives of “Invisible Animals.” The association notes, however, that there have been no fur farms in Bulgaria since 2025, making it easy to ban something that no longer exists. “The real test for the deputies will be the ban on cages for calves,” the organisation stated. In Europe Mink farming in Denmark will be phased out by August 2029, after the government decided to abandon plans to seek an exemption from a broader European ban on the activity, according to the BBC. Denmark is the world’s largest producer of mink fur, but the sector has declined as a result of bans introduced in various countries, the shrinking fur trade, and a previous outbreak of a COVID strain among the country’s mink population. The ban takes effect on 7 August next year, with a two-year transitional period for the gradual cessation of operations. Denmark dismantles its agricultural past: a radical pivot to green farming The article in Bulgarian by EUalive’s partner Sega can be found here . Caption: Raccoon dog raised for its fur [Humane World for Animals Europe]

noticias.titulo: Elecciones generales 2026
noticias.texto:
De 'La Revuelta' a Jordi Wild: el furor de los candidatos por conectar con el votante joven desde un perfil más humano
- Las entrevistas de humor y los formatos digitales permiten "humanizar" al candidato, apuntan los expertos
- Los partidos buscan conectar 'de tú a tú' para convencer a posibles abstencionistas o indecisos
En todas las elecciones hay una parte crítica a la hora de movilizar al electorado: es la más visceral, la que revuelve la emoción y la que conecta con el lado más humano del votante. Hacer sentir que el candidato es "uno de los nuestros" más allá de dar un perfil institucional o de gestor. Sobre todo, entre los jóvenes, que son más propensos tradicionalmente a ir a la abstención. Y eso lo tienen muy en cuenta los candidatos y, en especial, sus estrategas de comunicación, de cara a las generales del 29N. Todos han entrado en el juego y están priorizando las entrevistas en clave de humor (como La Revuelta), así como pódcast y formatos digitales (como el de Jordi Wild), más allá de los mítines y las entrevistas periodísticas.
"Son puntos clave de la campaña", explica a TVE Mariola Tàrrega Moltó, profesora de comunicación política de los Estudios de Ciencias de la Información y de la Comunicación de la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC). Argumenta que estos programas "tienen un formato de entretenimiento que es mejor recibido por las personas que quieren informarse sobre política que los formatos puramente informativos". En ellos, se permite dar un mensaje "más amable" y llegar "a un público diferente y con un tono más humano y de humor". Este tono, añade, "facilita la comprensión".
Hasta la fecha, el más activo en estos formatos ha sido el presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista, Pedro Sánchez. Tras una legislatura muy activo en TikTok e Instagram mostrando su lado más personal y sus recomendaciones musicales, ha participado últimamente en La Revuelta, El Perro Andaluz (ambos de TVE), The Wild Project y en el pódcast de Keep it Cutre, con una entrevista que pasó desapercibida porque se publicó justo antes de la tragedia ferroviaria en Urda (Toledo) el 28 de octubre.
Este mismo sábado aprovechaba el apodo 'La Peter', que le puso cariñosamente Candela Peña en La Revuelta, en su mítin en Palma de Mallorca. Ya lo hizo en 2023, dando la vuelta al insulto "perro" y convirtiéndolo en un signo de identidad, incluso con merchandising bajo el lema "Perro Sanxe".
También han pasado por la Revuelta Ada Colau (Frente Amplio), Irene Montero y Gabriel Rufián (Podemos y ERC, que fueron juntos), e incluso el líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, el único de la esfera de la derecha en acudir a este programa. Tras la entrevista, no exenta de polémica, canceló su entrevista al día siguiente en The Wild Project, por donde también han pasado, además de Sánchez, Alberto Núñez Feijóo (PP) y Colau. El líder del PP ha sido el único que, por ahora, ha ido a El Hormiguero, si bien ha rechazado el ofrecimiento de La Revuelta.
Se ha dicho de todo en estos programas: "Cuando tenía diez u once años me llevé algún petardo de la tienda"; "yo no sé inglés, pero mira, sé gobernar"; "me sale el punto cómico que tú has perdido en esta entrevista"; "venía del desierto, dejé la Alcaldía y recuperé la alegría de vivir"; "me preocupa que esté de moda ser un cabronazo"; "en campaña, necesidades vitales son comer, dormir, follar"; etc.
No es algo nuevo en esta campaña. Forma ya parte de la memoria colectiva la exvicepresidenta del Gobierno Soraya Sáenz de Santamaría bailando en El Hormiguero en 2015 y diciendo que le gustaba hacer de DJ, algo a lo que se animó al año siguiente en un mitin del PP. O cuando el entonces nuevo secretario general del PSOE Pedro Sánchez llamó en 2014 al presentador de Sálvame Jorge Javier Vázquez, en directo durante la grabación del programa, para pedir directamente su voto tras una polémica por los toros.
"Cualquier cosa que se pueda viralizar tiene mayor potencial de llegar a tus votantes"
Pero hay un factor diferencial decisivo en los tiempos que corren, y son las redes sociales y la forma en la que se consumen los contenidos. "Ya no se consume cuando se hace el programa, ni siquiera a través de la plataforma oficial, sino a través de los 'clips' (fragmentos) en redes sociales. Cualquier cosa que se pueda viralizar ahí tiene mayor potencial de llegar a tus votantes y sabemos que, en un panorama donde ahora no se consume tanta información en el formato lineal, puede haber una gran influencia", prosigue Tàrrega.
No todos los votantes están en redes sociales, claro está. Pero sí los jóvenes, aquellos de más de 18 años hasta los que están en la treintena o incluso la cuarentena.
En las elecciones de 2023, un Pedro Sánchez al que todos daban por acabado dio un vuelco a las encuestas logrando subir un escaño y pudiendo formar gobierno junto a Sumar. Entonces, la participación juvenil de los menores de 35 años fue del 66,5% (según el CIS postelectoral), una cifra notablemente alta para unas elecciones en julio.
La izquierda del bloque PSOE y Sumar concentró más de la mitad de ese voto joven. Algunos análisis de entonces ya hablaban de cómo la estrategia de la izquierda en pódcast (recordemos a Sánchez en La Pija y la Quinqui) y sus vídeos en redes como Tik Tok pudo evitar la abstención de los jóvenes progresistas desmovilizados tras el batacazo de las autonómicas y municipales dos meses antes.
"El votante joven es más proclive a abstenerse en el último momento"
"El votante joven es más proclive a abstenerse en el último momento o a desmovilizarse. Incluso, también, a cambiar de opción electoral", destaca Edu Bayón, consultor en comunicación política.
Con estos formatos de entrevista más distendidos, los votantes pueden "identificarse" con el candidato cuando habla "de temas mucho más amables o mundanos" como sus aficiones, sus grupos de música, los deportes que practican o cómo pasan su tiempo de ocio, prosigue Bayón. Esto no solo logra, añade, "humanizar", sino que permite una "horizontalidad", y es que el votante, sobre todo el joven, "le perciba (al candidato) como uno de los suyos".
Pero no todo es una cuestión de voluntad política, sino que apunta a que los candidatos a día de hoy se ven de alguna forma forzados a participar en ciertos formatos, sobre todo en aquellos que han nacido en Internet y que, como The Wild Project, han adquirido con el paso del tiempo un gran número de seguidores (7,5 millones de suscriptores en el caso del programa de Jordi Wild).
"Fue él quien lanzó la propuesta a los políticos y todos aceptaron rápidamente. La propia magnitud de quién está proponiendo la participación obliga o arrastra a los políticos a participar y eso es un hecho bastante destacable", prosigue.
Un hecho llamativo del programa de Jordi Wild es que en los últimos tiempos ha incorporado verificadores en directo, algo poco habitual en estos formatos y que suele responder más a entrevistas clásicas de televisión.
"El relato vence al dato"
Los expertos consultados coinciden en que en estos nuevos formatos "el relato vence al dato". El politólogo de la Universidad de Barcelona Jesús Palomar subraya que buena parte del público que sigue la política en internet "se informa por Instagram o por el influencer de turno que dice lo que sea sin contrastarlo". Y esto hace que las entrevistas de humor o en pódcast no periodísticos resulten más atractivas para los candidatos, al no ser repreguntados con datos incómodos.
También coinciden los expertos en que estos formatos funcionan muy bien porque la movilización en los últimos días de campaña llega por la vía "emocional". Precisamente, estudios como 'The Rationalizing Voter', de la Universidad de Cambridge (2013) demostró que el afecto hacia un líder o partido se activa en milisegundos de forma automática e inconsciente antes de que el votante recuerde ningún dato o propuesta programática.
"Casi nadie se lee un programa político ni vota solo en términos de interés material. La mayoría del voto es como el ser humano, muy emocional y muy identitario", recalca Palomar, que puntualiza que la emoción no siempre es la simpatía, sino también la aversión por el líder o el partido contrario.
Y más allá de los votantes, tampoco los programas de humor y de internet están exentos de mostrar signos de una u otra ideología, y de ahí las reticencias de algunos políticos a asistir a algunos de ellos. Y ahí está uno de los retos de la campaña: "Si un candidato es capaz de dominar el programa de la ideología contraria, es clave (...) Si sales airoso, los que ven la entrevista y están indecisos ven que eres humano. Y en los últimos años venimos de una gran deshumanización de la política".
Tàrrega pone el foco en el "carisma" del candidato. "El carismático siempre es más fácil que se adapte a los nuevos formatos y tiene mucho potencial, tanto para la tele como para las redes sociales (...) El formato actual de las redes sociales tiene su tono informal y coloquial, que puede ser más difícil" para otros con menos carisma, subraya. Y destaca que uno de los riesgos para los candidatos es, por un lado, que no sepa conectar con la audiencia. Por otro, es que "al bajar mucho al café de la calle puedes perder el perfil de gestor" y acabar "pareciendo el vecino del barrio y no alguien que tiene la capacidad de poder liderar el Estado".
En este difícil equilibrio, por ejemplo, está Feijóo, que ha criticado duramente la precampaña de Sánchez por sus bailes y su beso con su esposa, Begoña Gómez, en los mítines e incluso ha llegado a prometer que él no será un presidente que baile, cante o bese a su mujer en los actos de partido. Feijóo recalca su perfil de gestor, mientras en las redes sociales, el Partido Popular busca conectar con ese electorado joven presentándole en un vídeo al estilo 'anime' como un superhéroe que se impone a un Sánchez vestido de villano. Un vídeo que recuerda al de Lula da Silva en Brasil para las presidenciales de Brasil.
Con todo, asumiendo estos riesgos y oportunidades, los expertos concluyen que la estrategia de los candidatos busca un resultado claro en las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. "No van a dar la vuelta (a las encuestas) como para dar una mayoría absoluta a un partido, pero entran en este terreno sabiendo que se juegan una buena parte de los indecisos y de los abstencionistas", zanja Bayón.

noticias.titulo: Serie La Promesa avance semanal
noticias.texto:
Redescubriendo a Cecilia: la cantautora pionera, la rebelde, la hipersensible, la hija del diplomático
- El pasado 9 de noviembre se estrenó el documental Cecilia. Una luz de mañana
- Hablamos con el director, la hermana de la artista y su biógrafo
Cuando el 2 de agosto de 1976 Cecilia falleció en un accidente de coche en Colinas de Trasmonte (Zamora), a los 27 años, no murió "una brisa sin aire" sino un tornado de tonelaje popular y artístico excepcional. "Nada de nada", como cantaba en su clásico, fue todo lo contrario a lo que pasó, y medio siglo después un documental honra a la cantautora. Cecilia.Una luz de mañana se estrenó el pasado 9 de noviembre porque recuerden "Quien cada nueve de noviembre, como siempre sin tarjeta, le mandaba un ramito de violetas"...
Los autodestructivos Kurt Cobain, Amy Winehouse, Brian Jones, Janis Joplin, Jim Morrison o Jimi Hendrix son los miembros del trágicamente afamado club de los 27, vidas truncadas a una edad temprana pero suficiente para dejar un legado creativo que aguanta el paso de un tiempo que a ellos mismos les fue negado. Diferente causa pero similar destino fue el caso de Evangelina Sobredo, alias Cecilia por una canción de Simon & Garfunkel, porque ya había una Eva… y CBS dispuso. A ella no le entusiasmó la idea.
Hija de un embajador español en una familia liberal, su infancia y juventud las vivió entre Southampton, Filadelfia, Portugal o Jordania. El inglés fue su idioma primigenio y cuando volvió a la Península Ibérica tuvo que aprender un español que amó y que le llevó a componer unas canciones de envergadura poética y hasta confeccionar un disco sobre Valle Inclán truncado por su muerte. Imaginen una figura pop actual haciendo un proyecto así. Ah bueno, los Hidrogenesse con Álvaro Pombo, vale. Pero imaginen a Amaia, con quien se le han visto paralelismos por su popularidad y personalidad… ¿pero a que no?
¿Y qué escritores le gustaban aparte de Ramón María del Valle Inclán a esta poeta? “San Juan de la Cruz, Santa Teresa de Jesús o Virginia Woolf. También hay mucha influencia de James Joyce y, luego, mucha literatura española. Porque descubrir la literatura española para ella era como descubrir España. Piensa que sale de aquí cuando tiene 3 años y que cuando vuelve a estudiar Derecho en Madrid está descubriendo su propio país”, explica José Madrid, biógrafo de Cecilia.
¿Cuál hubiera sido su futuro artístico?
En este sentido, y nos anticipamos al típico cierre de artículo, la pregunta obligatoria cuando abordamos casos de muerte prematura en un creador. ¿Qué camino artístico habría transitado? Porque también pintaba. Y, siempre en modo especulativo, hay que apuntar "además de que era una gran lectora, creo que habría escrito novelas, estoy convencido. Sus canciones a veces son como una película de Berlanga o de Bardem. Como un Ramito de Violetas, por ejemplo, que es como un guion y que tiene un giro al final al descubrirte que era el marido el que la mandaba flores", hipotetiza el biógrafo.
"Tiene mucha razón José, que hubiera sido escritora, pero yo me quedo con lo que ella me dijo y les dijo a mis padres mientras estábamos tomando el té un día: 'Voy a dejar la discográfica y me voy a dedicar a hacer mis canciones'. '¿Y donde vas a cantar?', yo le dije. Me respondió: 'Muy fácil. Voy a buscar escenarios pequeños, cantar a la gente'". Ella quería volver al principio de su época universitaria, cuando cantaba en los colegios mayores”, responde la risueña Teresa, hermana de la artista, que añade que también pretendía convertirse en productora y "ayudar a gente joven a cantar y formarse en el mundo de la canción".
De hecho, como nos cuenta el director Chema de la Peña, la propia cantante señala sus planes en un documental con abundante material de archivo también de las típicas grescas con la discográfica por el clásico conflicto entre comercialidad y libertad: "Llevaba tantos desencantos, tantas peleas, que al final hubiera apostado a lo mejor por más dedicarse solo a la composición y hacer temas para los demás. No lo sabemos. Creo que ella, como también dice en el documental: 'Como buen signo Libra que soy, siempre estoy buscando un equilibrio que nunca aparece'".
Transgresora sin buscarlo
Cecilia fue una adelantada a tu tiempo, la primera cantautora española junto con Mari Trini (ella más anglófila, de los Beatles, Joan Baez y Bob Dylan; la segunda afrancesada), pero a la vez no pretendía ser una artista transgresora ni convertirse en la más 'cool' del país o algo así. Precisamente, ahí radica parte de su aura singular porque sin darse aires de especial reivindicaba la copla, el cuplé y la zarzuela y a la par abordaba temas pioneros como la polución en las ciudades, la violencia machista o el suicidio.
En el Cecilia 2, precisamente, su álbum más personal, aborda "los motivos para seguir viva". "Lo puedes ver también como un alegato a la vida y por eso también pasó la censura y no fue algo tan tan controvertido. Pero, efectivamente, ese disco tiene cosas de las que no hablaba nadie", apunta Madrid. "Yo siempre digo que ese es un disco místico y el más ceciliano", corrobora la hermana. Y zanja el biógrafo: "Es el disco en el que se abre en canal".
Hay que apuntar que este Cecilia 2 fue un 'regalo' de su discográfica por el petardazo de su debut homónimo, el de la portada con el guante de boxeo y que incluía Dama, Dama, que fue número 1, y tuvieron con esta apetencia de la artista más manga ancha, aunque fue un fracaso comercial que, a posteriori, con el tiempo, llegó a ser considerado una obra esencial de su carrera y entró incluso en los mejores 100 discos de la música española del siglo XX para la revista Rockdelux, por ejemplo.
España no fue un trauma
La llegada a España en plena dictadura no supuso para Cecilia y sus hermanos un choque cultural traumático. En su casa habían crecido en un ambiente de libertad y siguieron hablando de todo y cuestionando las cosas. "Mi madre nos había educado en ese rollo", recuerda Teresa, que evoca cómo una señora "que les vigilaba" les advertía de que tuvieran cuidado con lo que decían: "Que se aguanten". Aquella rebeldía formaba parte del carácter de todos los hermanos y no estaban dispuestos a renunciar a ella.
O cuando dejaron de ir a misa, su madre, profundamente religiosa (como en el fondo era Cecilia también, a su manera), se llevó un disgusto, pero su padre zanjó la cuestión con una defensa rotunda de la libertad individual: "No quiero hipócritas en mi familia. Si no quieren ir, ya sabrán por qué no van. Y si quieren volver, que vuelvan. Pero que hagan lo que les dé la gana". Su hermana recuerda a un hombre que "no le gustaba que la gente estuviera como un caballo amarrado, que no se puede mover ni el cuello".
Una Cecilia a la que a la vez vemos en el documental mostrar varias caras, quizá compatibles, aparte de descubrir que era querente a las palabrotas. "Soy tímida, me cuesta muchísimo decir que no, me horroriza decepcionar. Soy sensible y llorona, tengo muchos miedos y complejos", relata también y, a la par, confronta este descarnamiento o el de algunas letras bajo mínimos anímicos con una guerrera de desenvuelta confianza. ¿Tenía estas dos personalidades?
Fondo depresivo, neurótica, decidida y con carácter
La hermana aquí relata rauda una anécdota de cómo Eva (Cecilia) gracias a su brillante expediente académico y a su carácter decidido, se enfrentó a un funcionario franquista para conseguir que le reconocieran sus estudios previos en Inglaterra y evitar repetir un examen. También recuerda su paso por la Facultad de Derecho, donde dejó impresionado a un profesor especialmente exigente y consiguió la única matrícula de honor que concedió. ¿Entonces era ciclotímica? Porque se habla con dureza a sí misma y hasta se lo canta con que es "una brisa sin aire", que es "nada de nada", algo muy indie…
"Es sorprendente porque tú nunca verías a algún artista hoy por hoy reconocer ese tipo de cosas, por el culto al ego que hay. Creo que podían convivir las dos cosas. Me identifico mucho con esa valentía del tímido o del aparentemente tímido". Teresa suma: "Más que tímida era aparentemente... De tímida tenía cero, se sacaba un carácter... Era como mi hermano Ramón, que tenía un carácter también tremendo. Ellos tenían el carácter de mi abuelo Luis, que era muy bueno, pero el día que se enfadaban había que desaparecer".
De hecho, Cecilia era una persona de las que podía romper el cable del teléfono en un arrebato. Sobre todo si tenía "rollos malos" con la discográfica para "teledirigirla". "'Estos hijos de puta', decía. 'Pues esto tiene que ser así porque es una creación artística y autoral'. Y le pregunté: '¿Por qué no cedes?'. 'Porque mis canciones y mis letras son arte de largo plazo y no son single music. El Dúo Dinámico hace unas canciones soberbias y les salen así porque son unos cachondos mentales. Pero yo no soy así. Yo compongo lo que a mí me viene en mi interior y no me gusta que me impongan'".
"Indígena madrileña"
Y el biógrafo hace un apunte personal, para pulir el dibujo psicológico, sobre algo que le dijo Luis Gómez Escolar, quien fuera pareja sentimental de Cecilia: "Tenía un fondo depresivo muy potente, pero eso se ve en las canciones. Como todo ser humano tienes altos y bajos, si no no seríamos seres humanos". Y añade Teresa: "Chema el director capta una cosa genial en el documental y son las neuras de ella y de todas las hermanas, que somos muy neuróticas".
Hipersensible ("todo lo sentía a la máxima potencia y por eso tenemos las canciones que nos ha legado") pero sencilla a la vez, una cantautora muy popular que odiaba la fama, ¿Cecilia qué representó para la sociedad española de primeros de los 70? "Es una artista única, rompedora sin querer serlo. Es como una marciana que sale vestida de una forma que no salen vestidas las mujeres de esa época porque sale casi sin maquillaje y con sandalias. Ella decía que era una indígena madrileña”.
Para el director, es una pionera que abrió camino a las mujeres en la música española, hasta el punto de afirmar que "Rosalía no existiría sin Cecilia". Recuerda que, antes de ella, cantantes como Massiel, Rocío Jurado o Lola Flores eran principalmente intérpretes: "Mujeres que se presentaban como figuras de belleza y exuberancia, con un vestuario, unas canciones y una carrera musical diseñados por otros". Y Cecilia rompió con ese modelo en pleno franquismo: componía sus propios temas, decidía cómo vestirse y tomó las riendas de su trayectoria. "Fue la primera que decidió que se podía hacer".

noticias.titulo: Sánchez plantea el 29N como un referéndum "entre la buena política y la mala educación" y propone subir los impuestos a los fondos buitre
noticias.texto:
Sánchez plantea el 29N como un referéndum "entre la buena política y la mala educación" y propone subir los impuestos a los fondos buitre
- Rodeado de 5.500 asistentes en Alcorcón, en el sur de Madrid, ha desglosado el programa del PSOE
- Propone crear una nueva unión civil de convivencia y crear una prestación estatal por crianza
La lluvia fina pero constante en Alcorcón (Madrid) no ha evitado que este domingo por la mañana se hayan formado largas colas para acceder al polideportivo Los Cantos de la ciudad madrileña. El espacio, lleno a rebosar, ha recibido a Pedro Sánchez en pie. "Cada vez estamos más movilizados y las derechas tienen más miedo", ha gritado el speaker del PSOE para animar aún más a los presentes.
Pedro Sánchez ha observado un auditorio muy receptivo y ha querido aprovecharlo para hablarles antes de comenzar el mitin, un gesto del todo inusual. En una mano el micrófono y en la otra una bandera de España que no ha dejado de agitar. "Esta es nuestra bandera, la bandera de la Constitución Española; la bandera de la democracia; la de los derechos; de la igualdad; de las mujeres y sus derechos; la bandera de la diversidad territorial; de nuestros abuelos, padres y madres que lucharon por la democracia en nuestro país, la bandera de la fuerza de la gente".
Pedro Sánchez ha jugado este sábado en casa. Ha sido el primer gran acto de campaña que ha organizado la federación socialista madrileña (Sánchez es el número uno en la lista por Madrid) y han puesto toda la carne en el asador para que el acto fuera un lleno absoluto, con autobuses desde varios puntos de la región. De nuevo, centenares de personas se han quedado en la calle sin la posibilidad de acceder al recinto, mostrando cierta resignación tras más de una hora de espera.
La importancia de este acto también se ha evidenciado con la presencia de más de ocho ministros del actual Gobierno, entre ellos el ministro de Presidencia, Félix Bolaños; la titular de Defensa, Margarita Robles; la ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, o la ministra de Seguridad Social, Elma Saiz. También ha acudido los padres de Pedro Sánchez, sentados en segunda fila.
Ya en su intervención, el candidato del PSOE a la reelección ha dejado bien claro que estas elecciones se deben de tomar como un referéndum "entre la buena política y la mala educación", en referencia a las papeletas de PP y Vox. "La buena política es avanzar, la mala política es involucionar como proponen Feijóo y Abascal... Es refugiarse en el 'me gusta la fruta'. La buena educación no da fruta, da sus frutos", ha reivindicado.
"Esconden su mala gestión bajo la mala educación, y dicen 'me gusta la fruta' mientras dan 7.000 millones a una empresa privada como Quirón o intentan pagar un atizaco con siete millones de euros pagados por los madrileños", ha dicho, generando largos aplausos del público.
Sánchez también ha profundizado en sus críticas a Feijóo por no hablar inglés. "Alberto, estoy de acuerdo contigo que el presidente de Gobierno de España debe de saber inglés", un comentario que ha despertado muchas risas. "Ahora, en una entrevista de trabajo, a mucha gente joven se lo piden. ¿Cómo no lo va a tener el presidente del Gobierno de una gran nación como es España?", se ha preguntado
Sánchez desgrana algunas medidas del programa del PSOE
El PSOE ha escogido a Alcorcón, un antiguo feudo socialista, para presentar su programa electoral, acompañado de su candidato autonómico, el ministro Óscar López. Pese a ser una de las ciudades de las que se considera el "cinturón rojo" de Madrid y tener un ayuntamiento socialista con el apoyo de Más Madrid y un partido local, aquí el PP se impuso en las generales de 2023.
Entre las principales medidas que ha mencionado se encuentra la de subir los impuestos a los fondos buitre que tengan pisos vacíos o que los usen como apartamentos turísticos. Asimismo, su intención es que el parque público de vivienda represente el 6%, la media europea y "que no se vendan más las viviendas protegidas a los fondos buitres".
También ha explicado que los socialistas proponen nuevos permisos paternales con el 100% de retribución de la base reguladora para el cuidado de menores de 8 años durante cuatro semanas. El PSOE incluye en su programa, además, una nueva unión civil, que ya se encuentra en el código civil catalán y vasco, para que se pueda celebrar una unión de convivencia con alguien que no tenga que ser estrictamente pareja.
Sobre los autónomos, Sánchez ha prometido que "seguirá avanzando" para que coticen en base a los ingresos reales durante la próxima legislatura, y mantendrá la prestación por cese de actividad y por cuidados.
El candidato socialista a la reelección, además, se ha marcado otros objetivos a lograr en los próximos cuatro años, hasta 2030. "Hemos logrado que el 60% de la energía consumida provenga de las energías renovables. En 2030 queremos que sea el 80%", ha expresado. También ha dicho que quiere que "la tasa de paro sea de un dígito, del 8%" y que en la próximo legislatura "la brecha salarial entre hombres y mujeres se reduzca al 5%".
Sánchez también ha reiterado que si vuelve a gobernar blindará en la Constitución la revalorización de las pensiones en función del IPC y el derecho al aborto, medidas que ya había anunciado previamente.
Un muñeco de crochet, nuevo elemento de campaña
La campaña de los socialistas sigue con mítines como el de este domingo pero también sigue sumando nuevos elementos curiosos. En el mitin de Alcorcón ha aparecido un muñeco con la figura de Pedro Sánchez hecha de crochet.
Según explica el autor de este muñeco, lo ha realizado en 21 días e incluye una rosa tejida en las nalgas. Un vídeo recoge el momento en el que Sánchez ha recibido el presente, que ha respondido con risas tras conocer todos los detalles de su elaboración.
La organización ha repartido en el mitin de Alcorcón pegatinas con una fotografía del muñeco y el lema "¡Pedro Snchz, QHDP!", en referencia a la broma que él mismo realizó en una entrevista televisiva.
